items.title: Southern California Edison warns of potential wildfire-related power shutoffs
items.author: Varun Sahay
items.creator: Varun Sahay
items.summary: An Edison International-owned electric utility could shut off power for up to 245,700 customers in parts of Southern California to reduce wildfire risk, the largest number under consideration for a potential public safety outage this year.
items.body:
An Edison International-owned (EIX.N) electric utility could shut off power for up to 245,700 customers in parts of Southern California to reduce wildfire risk, the largest number under consideration for a potential public safety outage this year.
Southern California Edison said on Wednesday strong winds and dry conditions in portions of Los Angeles, Santa Barbara, Ventura, Kern and Tulare counties could increase wildfire risk between Wednesday and Friday.
Here are more details:
Southern California Edison has not yet decided whether to implement shutoffs and said the decision would be based on real-time weather and wildfire conditions
The utility said it monitors wind speeds, vegetation dryness and relative humidity when evaluating potential shutoffs
Southern California Edison uses about 2,000 weather stations, 200 wildfire cameras and ground patrols to monitor high fire-risk areas
If shutoffs are implemented, crews will inspect power lines and equipment before restoring service — a process that typically takes up to eight hours, but could be longer if damage is found or additional inspections are required
The utility said wildfire mitigation efforts include undergrounding power lines and installing covered conductors to reduce wildfire risk and the need for future shutoffs
"We have a responsibility to keep our community safe from the devastating impacts of wildfires," Southern California Edison spokesperson David Eisenhauer told Reuters
"PSPS (public safety power shutoff) significantly reduces the risk that equipment could start an ignition during extreme weather," Eisenhauer said

items.title: What is Starshield, SpaceX's military version of Starlink?
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Ukraine said on Wednesday that Elon Musk's SpaceX had restricted military-grade Starlink services, hampering Ukrainian drone strike missions and air defenses.
items.body:
Ukraine said on Wednesday that Elon Musk's [USN:L8N4600M6 TEXT:"SpaceX had restricted "military-grade" Starlink services"], hampering Ukrainian drone strike missions and air defenses.
The complaint has drawn renewed attention to the distinction between Starlink, SpaceX's commercial satellite internet service, and Starshield, a military version developed for the Pentagon. While Musk has said the two systems are separate, in many cases they share the same underlying satellite technology.
"Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government," Musk said on Wednesday in a post on X, adding that any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military or the president. "Starlink is a commercial service owned and controlled by SpaceX. Usage of Starlink is limited to civilian or defensive activities and cannot be used for offensive military action, as doing so would be inappropriate for a commercial company."
WHAT IS STARLINK? Starlink, the main profit engine of SpaceX (SPCX.O) , is a satellite internet network of more than 11,000 satellites that beam broadband service directly to user terminals about the size of a folded newspaper. Its roughly 13 million subscribers range from households and hikers to shipping companies and major airlines.
Since launching its first Starlink satellites in 2019 aboard reusable SpaceX rockets, the company has built a vast low-Earth-orbit constellation that blankets much of the planet, delivering faster connections than traditional communications satellites, which typically operate much farther from Earth and in far smaller numbers.
Starlink gave Ukraine a critical communications advantage early in the war, reshaping how militaries operate on the battlefield. But Musk has restricted Starlink for certain military uses while highlighting Starshield, a more secure network developed for government and military missions.
WHAT IS STARSHIELD? Starshield is a SpaceX business unit that develops military and intelligence satellite systems for the Pentagon.
While its missions are separate from Starlink's commercial broadband service, the distinction is not always clear-cut: Starshield's secure communications services use enhanced encryption and dedicated terminals, but rely on the vast Starlink constellation as their backbone.
Starshield leverages the technology, engineering and operational experiences of Starlink, according to SpaceX. In addition to secure communications, the company says the militarized version can also provide users with Earth observation and the ability to integrate sensors or other payloads.
The Pentagon, Starshield's largest customer, has spent billions of dollars on both Starlink and Starshield services. It has also bought dedicated Starshield satellites, including communications spacecraft for missile-warning missions and a spy constellation for the National Reconnaissance Office, Reuters reported in 2024.
Questions over the relationship between Starlink and Starshield have persisted since [USN:L1N31S38K TEXT:"Russia threatened Western satellites supporting Ukraine in 2022"]. SpaceX unveiled Starshield later that year, but the secrecy surrounding national security space programs has left the precise boundaries between the two systems opaque.
Those distinctions became a point of contention earlier this year when the [USN:L6N41W1B2 TEXT:"Pentagon clashed with SpaceX over higher prices for satellite services"] used by military drones during the Iran conflict, Reuters reported. SpaceX argued that some customers paying roughly $5,000 per terminal for Starlink should instead have been using a Starshield service costing about $25,000 per terminal.
[USN:L6N4290XG TEXT:"Britain has also adopted Starshield"]. Under that arrangement, the service uses the same satellite constellation, ground stations and terrestrial infrastructure as Starlink, but operates through dedicated terminals and separate network gateways, Britain’s defence ministry has told Reuters.
Other US partners are evaluating the system as well. New Zealand is doing a trial of Starshield to assess its usefulness for military operations, the New Zealand Defence Force previously told Reuters.

items.title: É montagem vídeo de Lula defendendo prender trabalhadores
items.author: Reuters Fact Check
items.creator: Reuters Fact Check
items.summary: Um vídeo de um discurso do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) foi adulterado para simular que ele defendeu prender trabalhadores e proteger criminosos. A montagem inverte a ordem das palavras do candidato à reeleição.
items.body:
Um vídeo de um discurso do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) foi adulterado para simular que ele defendeu prender trabalhadores e proteger criminosos. A montagem inverte a ordem das palavras do candidato à reeleição.
Estes são os principais detalhes:
O vídeo editado, que circula no Facebook , indica que Lula afirmou que o novo lema de sua campanha é “para o trabalhador, a prisão; para o bandido, a proteção”.
As imagens são de um discurso do presidente em uma plenária com parlamentares no último dia 7.
A transmissão ao vivo do pronunciamento no canal de Lula no YouTube e registros na imprensa mostram que o presidente defendeu proteger trabalhadores e prender criminosos, e não o contrário.
“E o nosso lema é o seguinte: para o povo trabalhador, a proteção; para o bandido, a prisão”, disse Lula ao mencionar propostas de campanha para a segurança pública.
Veredicto: Alterado digitalmente. Lula defendeu prender criminosos e proteger trabalhadores, e não o contrário.
Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. Envie sugestões de checagem via WhatsApp pelo número (11) 91599-9278. Leia mais sobre nosso trabalho de checagens de afirmações nas redes sociais aqui .

items.title: Guyanese opposition leader arrested after shots fired outside home of police official
items.author: Kemol King
items.creator: Kemol King
items.summary: Guyanese opposition leader Azruddin Mohamed and two other men have been arrested following an exchange of gunfire outside the home of a senior police officer who is testifying in a U.S. extradition case against Mohamed, the South American country's government and police said.
items.body:
Guyanese opposition leader Azruddin Mohamed and two other men have been arrested following an exchange of gunfire outside the home of a senior police officer who is testifying in a U.S. extradition case against Mohamed, the South American country's government and police said.
US prosecutors allege Mohamed and his father Nazar Mohamed conspired to commit fraud and launder money through their gold exporting firm, Mohamed’s Enterprise, to enrich themselves and defraud the government of Guyana. The two men, who were indicted in Florida, have denied wrongdoing and are contesting their [USN:L6N3YR0WY TEXT:"extradition proceedings"] in court.
The younger Mohamed has accused the government of persecuting him because of his entry into politics. His office on Wednesday denied possession of the firearm involved in the incident, accused police of planting it and alleged the three men were assaulted and threatened.
Mohamed and the other men were arrested overnight on Tuesday after Senior Superintendent of Police, Prem Narine, who is testifying in the extradition proceedings, observed a vehicle passing his residence. The vehicle later returned, according to a Tuesday statement from the Guyana Police Force, and Narine heard what he believed to be a gunshot as the vehicle approached.
Narine took cover, the statement said, and fired several rounds towards the car, which drove away. Officers later intercepted the vehicle, arresting Mohamed and the other men traveling in it. A search uncovered a firearm and ammunition, the police said.
The government said in a separate statement on Tuesday that Mohamed and his companions had been filming Narine’s residence. It alleged that shots came from their vehicle and said the gun the police found was unlicensed.
Mohamed's office described the shooting as an assassination attempt against Narine. Members of his We Invest in Nationhood party held a press conference on Wednesday to protest what they said was Mohamed's treatment by police. The party said he remains in custody.
Mohamed, who has had multiple run-ins with the police since his extradition case began, was elected opposition leader in January. We Invest in Nationhood became the [USN:L2N3UU00K TEXT:"top opposition force"] in parliament in the 2025 general election, winning 16 of 65 seats.

items.title: TD, BMO among 9 banks named in U.S. banking discrimination report
items.author: The Canadian Press
items.summary: A U.S. banking regulator has identified Bank of Montreal and TD Bank, along with seven other lenders, in a report about debanking and limiting access to financial services for certain U.S. customers ...
items.body: A U.S. banking regulator has identified Bank of Montreal and TD Bank, along with seven other lenders, in a report about debanking and limiting access to financial services for certain U.S. customers due to their political beliefs. The U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency released a report based on findings from a supervisory review of debanking activities at nine of the largest banks it oversees, based on 100,000 complaints at OCC-regulated institutions. The OCC says its review was conducted after an executive order by U.S. President Donald Trump, signed in August of last year, stipulating that Americans should not be denied access to financial services due to religious or political beliefs. Jonathan Gould, the comptroller of the currency, says the named banks “denied, debanked and discriminated against customers and lawful businesses.” TD did not immediately respond to a request for comment, while BMO referred The Canadian Press to a statement from the Bank Policy Institute. The institute, a U.S. industry advocacy group, says that it supports fair access to banking services and has been “working to ensure that government regulations and policies enable banks to serve law-abiding customers.” This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 14, 2026. Daniel Johnson, The Canadian Press

items.title: US midterm elections: What election officials fear Trump could do before and after Election Day
items.author: Ravi Hari
items.summary: The investigation, based on interviews with more than 50 election officials, voting experts and election lawyers, examines how the Trump administration could test the limits of federal authority before and after Election Day.
items.body: US President Donald Trump could disrupt the 2026 midterm elections through a series of actions ranging from allegations of voter fraud and federal investigations to immigration enforcement near polling places and disputes over election results, according to a Reuters investigation.Reuters said it interviewed more than 50 election officials, voting experts and election lawyers, and reviewed Trump's public statements, court filings and federal agency actions to identify nine potential flashpoints before and after Election Day.The November midterm elections will determine control of the US Congress and several key state offices.Here are the nine key risks to the US midterm elections identified by the Reuters investigation report.1. Trump alleges election fraud or compromised voting machinesTrump could renew unsubstantiated claims of voter fraud, illegal voting or manipulated voting machines. Reuters noted that similar allegations following the 2020 election fuelled efforts to overturn his defeat and led to harassment of election workers. Experts say such claims could trigger legal challenges even if they are subsequently disproved.2. Pressuring election officials to change or cancel resultsThe administration could pressure state officials, legislators or election authorities to reject certified results or delay certification based on fraud allegations. Reuters cited Trump's efforts to overturn his 2020 defeat, including his call to Georgia's secretary of state to find enough votes to reverse the result.3. Seizing ballots or voting equipmentFederal agents could seek court-approved warrants or subpoenas to obtain ballots, voting machines and election records. Such seizures could disrupt vote counting, compromise the chain of custody and delay certification. Reuters cited the FBI's January raid on election offices in Georgia's Fulton County, where agents seized records from the 2020 election.4. Federal election monitors interfering with votingThe Justice Department plans to deploy 1,000 election monitors, nearly twice the 590 deployed in 2024. While the department says they will protect voting rights and ensure compliance with federal law, some officials fear monitors could exceed their traditional role by seeking access to voting equipment or interviewing voters.5. ICE presence near polling sitesImmigration enforcement operations near polling places could discourage people from voting, particularly in immigrant communities and Democratic-leaning areas. Legal experts say deploying armed federal agents directly at polling stations would likely violate federal law, although immigration agents could conduct operations nearby.6. Troops deployed at polling placesTrump could seek to invoke the Insurrection Act to justify military deployment by citing alleged election-related unrest or interference. Experts warn that troops near polling stations could intimidate voters and suppress turnout. Federal laws restrict military involvement in domestic law enforcement and prohibit voter intimidation.7. Declaring a national emergencyTrump could declare a national emergency over alleged voter fraud or foreign interference to justify greater federal involvement in elections, potentially including demands for hand-counting ballots. Legal experts say emergency powers would not allow him to take over election administration, which largely falls under state authority, but such a move could trigger litigation and delays.8. Federal investigations and charges against election officialsThe Justice Department could investigate or prosecute election administrators over alleged failures to prevent noncitizens from voting or maintain accurate voter rolls. Officials fear that subpoenas, interviews and document demands could drain resources and intimidate election workers, even without convictions.9. Congress refusing to seat election winnersRepublican congressional leaders could face pressure to delay or challenge the seating of Democratic winners in closely contested races. Although legal scholars consider outright refusal to seat certified winners unlikely to succeed, delayed certifications and unresolved disputes could leave seats vacant when the new Congress convenes on January 3, potentially affecting control of the House.

items.title: Former portfolio manager sues Fidelity after leaving for Michael Dell's family office
items.author: Suzanne McGee
items.creator: Suzanne McGee
items.summary: A former semiconductor fund manager at Fidelity Investment Management has sued its parent company FMR, claiming it refused to pay him a "multimillion-dollar" compensation package after he joined DFO Management, the family office of billionaire Dell Technologies founder Michael Dell.
items.body:
A former semiconductor fund manager at Fidelity Investment Management has sued its parent company FMR, claiming it refused to pay him a "multimillion-dollar" compensation package after he joined DFO Management, the family office of billionaire Dell Technologies (DELL.N) founder Michael Dell.
The suit, filed by Adam Benjamin in the Suffolk Division of the Superior Court of Massachusetts, alleges that after Fidelity executives failed to persuade him to stay at the firm, the company "turned on a dime" and terminated him on July 10 of this year. Fidelity then imposed a non-compete clause, causing him to forfeit a compensation package totaling in the millions of dollars.
"Rather than protecting any legitimate business interests, the provisions are being broadly misused by Fidelity as a retention tool or improper barrier/deterrent to" Benjamin's ability to pursue other professional opportunities, the lawsuit alleges.
Fidelity declined to comment on the lawsuit, which was filed on Friday. Neither Benjamin nor his lawyers could be reached for comment.
Non-compete agreements are common in the asset management industry.
Benjamin managed the $48 billion Fidelity Select Semiconductors Portfolio, which is up 58% so far this year, compared to 13.3% for the S&P 500 (.SPX) index.
Its average annual return of 37.4% over the last five years puts it in the top percentile of all comparable funds rated by Morningstar, which awarded the fund five stars and a gold medalist rating, its top score.
Benjamin began working at DFO on October 1, the lawsuit said. He alleged that Fidelity's withholding of compensation rests on the false claim that he was joining a competitor. He said he has never worked for Fidelity's own family office business.

items.title: US judge won't block Trump order targeting DEI by federal contractors
items.author: Daniel Wiessner
items.creator: Daniel Wiessner
items.summary: A federal judge declined on Wednesday to block an effort by President Donald Trump to eliminate diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives by companies that do business with the US government.
items.body:
A federal judge declined on Wednesday to block an effort by President Donald Trump to eliminate diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives by companies that do business with the US government.
US District Judge Adam Abelson in Baltimore, Maryland, said that groups representing university faculty and minority business owners had failed to show [USN:L1N40S0IR TEXT:"a March executive order"] by the Republican president was too broad.
Trump's order bars [USN:FWN40E0ZQ TEXT:""racially discriminatory DEI activities""] by federal contractors and requires them to certify their compliance in writing. Businesses that do not comply could lose contracts and be investigated for violating the federal False Claims Act.
The groups in their lawsuit claim that Trump's order wrongly presumes that all DEI amounts to illegal racial discrimination and extends to speech protected by the US Constitution. But Abelson said its definition of unlawful conduct was narrower.
"The Contractors Order only prohibits contractors from engaging in conduct that is already prohibited by federal law: intentional discrimination on the basis of race or ethnicity," wrote Abelson, an appointee of President Joe Biden , a Democrat.
The judge denied the groups' motion to block Trump's order pending the outcome of the lawsuit, which was filed in April.
Democracy Forward, a progressive legal group that represents the plaintiffs, and the US Department of Justice did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Trump's order is also being challenged by 19 Democratic-led states and Washington, DC, in [USN:L1N42I0ZX TEXT:"a lawsuit in the same court"]. That case seeks to block federal agencies from altering contracts to comply with Trump's order.
Many of the largest US businesses, from defense and tech companies to food service providers and logistics firms, are federal contractors, and some companies primarily depend on the government for work.
Civil rights advocates say DEI practices help address historic inequities for marginalized groups like women, LGBTQ people and ethnic minorities.
But Trump and many conservatives cast DEI [USN:L8N42O1L3 TEXT:"as anti-merit and discriminatory"] against groups like white people and men, and his administration has moved to eradicate it from government, higher education and the private sector.
Trump has [USN:L1N3Z20XX TEXT:"banned DEI programs by federal agencies"] and repealed a 1965 executive order requiring federal contractors to take affirmative action to hire minorities and women.

items.title: Bond trading weakens for US banks as interest rate volatility affects investors
items.author: Tatiana Bautzer
items.creator: Tatiana Bautzer
items.summary: A steep selloff in the bond market showed up in Wall Street bank earnings during the last quarter, with some banks showing weaker fixed income trading as high interest rate volatility during the quarter curbed demand for transactions.
items.body:
A steep [USN:L8N45N0KW TEXT:"selloff in the bond market"] showed up in Wall Street bank earnings during the last quarter, with some banks showing weaker fixed income trading as high interest rate volatility during the quarter curbed demand for transactions.
During the quarter, Treasury yields reached [USN:L6N45S11R TEXT:"multi-decade highs"] with some days showing abrupt moves in the market as investors repriced their expectations for where interest rates will go.
At Morgan Stanley, revenues from fixed income, currencies and commodities trading (FICC) fell 7% in the quarter from a year earlier. [USN:L4N45Z0V1 TEXT:"At JPMorgan"], the drop was 4% and at [USN:L4N4600WF TEXT:"Bank of America"], 17%. [USN:L4N45Z0U6 TEXT:"Goldman Sachs"] had flat revenues with FICC trading. Citi was the odd one out, increasing its revenue 4% from a year earlier.
"Interest rates rose pretty furiously throughout the third quarter, and it was unexpected versus where the market was in the second quarter", said Morgan Stanley Chief Financial Officer Sharon Yeshaya. There was less demand for structured transactions and the widening of credit spreads was a challenge to investors that have bond portfolios.
Benchmark 10-year yields showed their [USN:L6N45M19U TEXT:"biggest quarterly rise since 2009"] at the end of September.
"Reduced client activity and changing market conditions, including a major shift in interest rates, significantly affected our leading FICC businesses, including credit, mortgages and municipals," according to Bank of America Chief Financial Officer Alastair Borthwick.
At Citigroup, most of the 4% growth in FICC trading revenue came from foreign exchange business and spread products. Citi CEO Jane Fraser told analysts rates revenue "was pressured by the trading environment, but we saw good growth in forex and spread products, both stable revenue streams."
Another effect of [USN:L1N45U12M TEXT:"rising long-term yields"] on the banks' balance sheets was the higher volume of unrealized losses in securities portfolios.
[USN:L4N4600XY TEXT:"Bank of America, for example"], showed unrealized losses on its bond portfolio - mortgage-backed securities and US Treasury, government-agency bonds - at $109 billion in the quarter ended September, up from $85 billion at the end of June, as bond yields rose in the last quarter.
The bulk of these securities were in held-to-maturity segment, which the bank does not intend to sell.
EQUITIES SHINE The results contrasted with that from equities trading desks, which brought eye-popping revenue growth in the quarter. At Goldman Sachs, equity trading revenue rose 72%, with higher revenues in derivatives and financing. Morgan Stanley equity revenues grew 41% and JPMorgan's, 49%. Bank of America and Citi had the lowest equity trading revenues growth, 11% and 14%, respectively.
Oppenheimer analyst Chris Kotowski sees increased risk in the reliance on equity revenues, that may be volatile. "We do fear that there is an 'easy come, easy go' risk with these revenues," he wrote in a note to clients.

items.title: Dinamarca diz que exploração de recursos pelos EUA na Groenlândia precisa respeitar leis locais
items.author: Louise Rasmussen
items.creator: Louise Rasmussen
items.summary: O Ministério das Relações Exteriores da Dinamarca afirmou nesta quarta-feira que, caso os EUA desejassem explorar os recursos da Groenlândia, teriam que fazê-lo dentro do marco da legislação da ilha ártica, acrescentando que o acordo assinado no mês passado entre as três partes não alterou essa situação.
items.body:
O Ministério das Relações Exteriores da Dinamarca afirmou nesta quarta-feira que, caso os EUA desejassem explorar os recursos da Groenlândia, teriam que fazê-lo dentro do marco da legislação da ilha ártica, acrescentando que o acordo assinado no mês passado entre as três partes não alterou essa situação.
O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, afirmou nesta quarta-feira que uma “exploração em grande escala de petróleo, gás e minerais” estava prestes a começar na Groenlândia — uma declaração polêmica sobre um território que tem resistido aos seus esforços para controlá-lo e proibiu novas perfurações em busca de petróleo bruto.
Trump descreveu a ilha ártica dinamarquesa, administrada por um governo semiautônomo, como “nossa nova e bela Groenlândia” em uma postagem nas redes sociais que elogiava o que ele chamou de ganhos dos EUA decorrentes de um acordo de segurança assinado em setembro.
O Ministério das Relações Exteriores da Dinamarca afirmou em comunicado que “o acordo não concede aos investidores dos EUA qualquer tratamento preferencial em comparação com investidores de outros países da Otan, da União Europeia e de parceiros da Otan no que diz respeito ao acesso aos recursos naturais da Groenlândia”.
O gabinete do primeiro-ministro da Groenlândia se recusou a comentar a declaração de Trump, enquanto o Ministério de Recursos Minerais da Groenlândia não respondeu imediatamente aos pedidos de comentário.

items.title: Biocon settles Roche's US patent lawsuit over proposed breast-cancer drug copy
items.author: Blake Brittain
items.creator: Blake Brittain
items.summary: Roche's Genentech has settled a US lawsuit against Indian biopharmaceutical company Biocon over its proposed biosimilar of Genentech's blockbuster breast-cancer drug Perjeta, Biocon said Wednesday.
items.body:
Roche's (ROPC.S) Genentech has settled a US lawsuit against Indian biopharmaceutical company Biocon (BION.NS) over its proposed biosimilar of Genentech's blockbuster breast-cancer drug Perjeta, Biocon said Wednesday.
Biocon said in a statement that the settlement gives it the "earliest licensed launch dates" for a Perjeta biosimilar, allowing the company to launch its Pebrilzo in the first quarter of 2027 in the UK and European Union, and the third quarter of 2028 in the United States
The release said that other terms of the agreement are confidential
Biosimilars are versions of biologic drugs that are comparable to generics of traditional pharmaceuticals. Unlike traditional drugs, complex biologic drugs are made from living cells and cannot be copied exactly
Genentech's biologic Perjeta was Switzerland-based Roche's sixth-best-selling drug last year, earning it nearly CHF 2.97 billion ($3.67 billion) in revenue worldwide, according to a company report
Genentech [USN:L6N43W11Z TEXT:"sued Biocon"] in New Jersey earlier this year, alleging Biocon's biosimilar would infringe its patents
The court dismissed the lawsuit on Wednesday at Genentech's request
Biocon did not respond to Genentech's allegations in court
The case is Genentech Inc v. Biocon Biologics Inc, US District Court for the District of New Jersey, No. 2:26-cv-09585
For Genentech: Michael Morin of Latham & Watkins
For Biocon: Jeanna Wacker of Kirkland & Ellis
Read more:
[USN:L6N43W11Z TEXT:"Roche sues Biocon over proposed breast-cancer drug copy"]

items.title: As Ukraine struggles with Starlink and US satellite data, Europe has no quick fix
items.author: Vaishnavi Hajari, Gianluca Lo Nostro, Cassell Bryan-Low
items.creator: Vaishnavi Hajari, Gianluca Lo Nostro, Cassell Bryan-Low
items.summary: As Ukraine reported problems with Starlink satellite internet terminals and US data that warns of Russian ballistic missile attacks, Kyiv also faced the harsh reality that its European allies cannot offer any ready-made alternatives.
items.body:
As Ukraine [USN:L8N4600M6 TEXT:"reported problems"] with Starlink satellite internet terminals and US data that warns of Russian ballistic missile attacks, Kyiv also faced the harsh reality that its European allies cannot offer any ready-made alternatives.
Ukrainian officials said on Wednesday the functioning of Starlink’s military-grade service Starshield had been interrupted when terminals were moving at high speed, hampering Ukrainian drones for attack missions and air defence.
Separately, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said that, for the second night running, Ukraine had received no warning from its partners of a Russian ballistic missile attack on Kyiv.
The reasons for the difficulties were not immediately clear but followed another souring of relations between US President Donald Trump and Ukraine, after Trump announced a deal to waive sanctions on Russian diesel and called for Zelenskiy to be replaced.
Trump said on Tuesday that the United States was still sharing intelligence with Ukraine. Elon Musk and his SpaceX company had no immediate comment on Ukraine’s assertions.
European countries have voiced strong support for Ukraine and Zelenskiy. But the problems with vital data highlighted that Ukraine and Europe depend heavily on US systems for both low-orbit satellite communications — provided by SpaceX via Starlink — and space-based infrared sensing that feeds into early-warning systems.
A US satellite constellation called the Space-Based Infrared System provides early missile warnings.
“That is fairly unique and … what basically that can detect is the heat generated by missiles as they're launched,” said Marc DeVore, an associate fellow at think tank Chatham House. “There is nothing equivalent in Europe.”
NO SIMPLE STARLINK SWAP FOR UKRAINE, EUROPE As for Starlink, Europe does not have a ready-made alternative that Ukrainian soldiers could attach to their drones, although European governments and companies are working on long-term options.
Shares in European satellite operator Eutelsat [USN:L6N4600QK TEXT:"soared"] on Wednesday following news of Ukraine's difficulties with Starshield, fuelled by investor bets that European providers could benefit from growing strains between Washington and Kyiv.
But Christian Freiherr von der Ropp, an independent satellite consultant, said Eutelsat's OneWeb network was [USN:L5N3PN1Q8 TEXT:"not well suited"] to wartime use.
"Its current constellation remains rooted in an outdated architecture and technology conceived a decade ago, without any evolution of its underlying design," he said.
"Capacity and performance constraints, combined with the cost, weight, bulk and power consumption of its user terminals, limit its suitability for frontline applications."
Eutelsat did not respond to a request for comment.
Von der Ropp also said switching networks would require replacing thousands of terminals, as Starlink and Starshield terminals use proprietary technology and could not simply connect to OneWeb.
Bohdan Sas, co-founder of Ukrainian defence technology startup Buntar Aerospace, said the sudden interruption to Starshield services "highlights to almost every end user both in Ukraine and abroad you can’t rely solely on one solution that can be switched off.”
“You need to have some kind of sovereign capabilities," he added, so that "you are not subject to somebody’s mood today.”
Fears of over-reliance on US defence technology have grown in Europe in recent years, as Trump has threatened to quit the NATO military alliance just as European leaders see Russia posing the greatest threat to the continent in decades.
European Defence Commissioner Andrius Kubilius said at a conference hosted by Politico in Brussels on Wednesday that the continent was "quite dependent on American space capabilities.”
“The answer to that situation is to develop our own capabilities,” he added, mentioning the European Union's planned satellite constellation IRIS² and urging European countries to work together to avoid frustration.
But that project is years from becoming operational even if everything goes according to plan, causing frustration among European government officials. Germany is developing its own military satellite constellation.

上昇して取引を終えた。ＦＴＳＥ１００種は反発。米インフレ指標を受けてポンドが対ドルで下落したことが好感され、輸出関連株が買われた。中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数も０．０９％高と続伸した。

一方、金などの値下がりで貴金属株指数 は３．５３％安。銀行株指数 は０．５８％下落した。

９月の米消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）は前年同月からの伸び率が加速し、市場予想を上回った。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞ 

小幅に反発して取引を終えた。半導体関連企業による強気な需要見通しを受け、人工知能（ＡＩ）を巡る懸念が和らいだ。

２０２６年７─９月期決算を発表したオランダの半導体製造装置メーカーＡＳＭＬホールディングは１．２％高。２９、３０年の発注に向けて顧客から関心が寄せられていると明らかにし、需要が堅調に推移する見通しが示された。

ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種ヘルスケア株指数は２．３１％高。ベルギーでの人員削減を発表した製薬大手ＧＳＫは３．６％上昇した。

一方、資源株指数は１．１８％安。ＪＰモルガンが目標株価を引き下げた貴金属採掘フレスニヨは４．６％下落した。

デンマークの風力発電大手オーステッドは３．９％安。米国の洋上風力発電所事業への懸念から、売られた。スウェーデンの銀行ＳＥＢは４．６％安。

ブレント原油先物価格は高値圏で推移。インフレへの懸念から、市場は欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）が１２月会合で追加利上げに踏み切るとの観測を強めている。

また、９月の米消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）は前年同月からの伸び率が加速し、市場予想を上回った。

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞　

域内国債利回りが上昇した。米国のインフレ加速で連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）の追加利上げ観測が強まり、米債利回りが上昇した動きに追随した。

米労働省労働統計局が発表した９月の米消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）は前月比０．６％、前年比では３．７％上昇し、前月の０．４％と３．４％上昇から加速した。ガソリン価格の急騰を背景に伸びが加速し、１０月中の米利上げの可能性が再び意識される状況となった。

クインテット・プライベート・バンクのチーフストラテジスト、ダニエレ・アントヌッチ氏は「総合とコアの双方でインフレが加速したことは、物価上昇圧力の持続性が強まっていることを示唆する」と指摘。「堅調な成長と相まって、これはわれわれがＦＲＢが年内の追加利上げに踏み切ると予想する理由の一つだ」と述べた。 

米国経済の規模と重要性、ＦＲＢが他の中央銀行に及ぼす影響力を踏まえると、米金融政策を巡る見通しは他の世界の債券市場にも影響を与える傾向がある。

米ＣＰＩを受けて米債券利回りが上昇する中、ドイツ１０年債利回りもこれに追随し、２ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）上昇の３．４８１％となった。

独仏１０年債利回り格差は約１４０ｂｐ。１０月序盤には一時１５８ｂｐ超まで拡大していた。欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）のラガルド総裁は１４日、フランスは財政健全化を通じて自国の債務問題を解決すべきだと述べ、ＥＣＢによる債券市場への介入観測を事実上けん制した。  

ＥＣＢは今年、２５ｂｐの利上げを２回実施している。短期金融市場は１２月の理事会までに追加利上げが実施されるとの見方を完全に織り込んでいる。

米労働省労働統計局が発表した９月の米消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）は前月比０．６％、前年比では３．７％上昇し、前月の０．４％と３．４％上昇から加速した。ガソリン価格の急騰を背景に伸びが加速し、１０月中の米利上げの可能性が再び意識される状況となった。

クインテット・プライベート・バンクのチーフストラテジスト、ダニエレ・アントヌッチ氏は「総合とコアの双方でインフレが加速したことは、物価上昇圧力の持続性が強まっていることを示唆する」と指摘。「堅調な成長と相まって、これはわれわれがＦＲＢが年内の追加利上げに踏み切ると予想する理由の一つだ」と述べた。 

米国経済の規模と重要性、ＦＲＢが他の中央銀行に及ぼす影響力を踏まえると、米金融政策を巡る見通しは他の世界の債券市場にも影響を与える傾向がある。

米ＣＰＩを受けて米債券利回りが上昇する中、ドイツ１０年債利回りもこれに追随し、２ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）上昇の３．４８１％となった。

独仏１０年債利回り格差は約１４０ｂｐ。１０月序盤には一時１５８ｂｐ超まで拡大していた。欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）のラガルド総裁は１４日、フランスは財政健全化を通じて自国の債務問題を解決すべきだと述べ、ＥＣＢによる債券市場への介入観測を事実上けん制した。  

ＥＣＢは今年、２５ｂｐの利上げを２回実施している。短期金融市場は１２月の理事会までに追加利上げが実施されるとの見方を完全に織り込んでいる。

items.title: US stocks: AI shares tumble, erasing $80 billion as hot US inflation fuels rate fears
items.author: Reuters
items.summary: Amid rising inflation, major AI firms like CoreWeave and Dell Technologies experienced significant stock price drops, losing around $80 billion in market value. Increased US interest rates have investors worried about the borrowing hurdles faced by less profitable firms within the sector. Even with the strong performance of giants like Nvidia and Microsoft, skepticism remains high, reminiscent of the dot-com era's cautionary tales.
items.body: Major AI stocks slumped on Wednesday following the latest hot US inflation report, highlighting investor concern about the risks posed by rising borrowing costs in this capital-intensive sector.Among the leading decliners were data center operator CoreWeave, which fell 16%, AI infrastructure provider Nebius, off 11%, cloud computing giant Oracle, down 9%, and AI server seller Dell Technologies, down 11%. Together the declines erased some $80 billion of market value.The declines reflect the impact of tightening financial conditions, as well as the outsize gains scored by some of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom. Barclays on Wednesday downgraded Dell and two other enterprise hardware stocks, noting that Dell shares have quadrupled this year - part of an AI-fueled investor binge that has resulted in 16 stocks in the S&P 500 technology sector at least doubling this year, according to Reuters calculations.Concern over rising borrowing costs also weighed on Wednesday's other big decliners. Selling has been particularly intense in CoreWeave, which has issued $22 billion of bonds and $26 billion of loans, according to LSEG data. A CoreWeave bond that was issued in June yielding 9.625% recently yielded 15%. We're getting a whole lot of information suggesting that the largest AI companies may not be generating the earnings or revenue people anticipated, and I think that makes everyone nervous about companies like CoreWeave, said Kim Forrest, chief investment officer at Bokeh Capital Partners.Coreweave Chief Executive Officer Mike Intrator said in an internal memo the market is acting irrationally and that he remains confident in the AI cloud company, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday.Wednesday's rout is the latest sign of a market struggling to come to grips with the implications of high inflation at a time when AI-fueled corporate borrowing has helped push up global interest rates.Investors generally remain sanguine on the sector in part because its largest players, from chip maker Nvidia to the so-called hyperscalers - primarily Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Amazon - are highly profitable and widely perceived as well managed, despite concerns about debt.But higher rates will make borrowing and building costlier, a fact that is likely to hit unprofitable and less-profitable firms first. On Wednesday, US interest rates rose following the hot inflation report, pushing the 30-year yield as high as 5.63% before rates pulled back sharply in the afternoon. I do think long rates above 5% and creeping towards 6% is a problem for the marginal borrower, I'll call them, said Ross Mayfield, investment strategy analyst at Baird, in an interview with Reuters. It gets a lot harder for the tiers below the kind of big four hyperscalers. The Nasdaq was down 2% on Wednesday afternoon, with Alphabet and the other major hyperscalers mostly down between around 2%. SpaceX, another major AI player, was down 3%. I guess it's grown to a group of five now. SpaceX has kind of joined the party here to join in with like Meta and Microsoft and Google and Amazon, said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management. Those five are spending like 75% of the money that's being invested in data centers here in the country. And those five are obviously putting all their profits and then some into these data centers and the returns they're generating from those are really good. Despite the strong economics of these firms and their investments, Ellerbroek said it's not surprising that investors remain skeptical about the AI buildout, in part because of the busts that have preceded this one, particularly the dot-com meltdown that started in 2000. This select group of companies is driving most of the growth in the economy and the stock market, and they're investing so, so aggressively and investors just aren't really willing to pay for it or fully buy in to the extent that we saw in the late 90s or whatever when investors kind of lost their minds, Ellerbroek said. Investors have definitely not lost their minds. They're being very cautious and I think selective.

items.title: Barcola bags hat-trick as Liverpool thrash LASK 6-3
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Liverpool's Bradley Barcola scored his first goals for the club with a hat-trick as they swept aside Champions League newcomers LASK 6-3 on Wednesday, spoiling the Austrian side's first home game in Europe's elite club competition.
items.body:
Liverpool's Bradley Barcola scored his first goals for the club with a hat-trick as they swept aside Champions League newcomers LASK 6-3 on Wednesday, spoiling the Austrian side's first home game in Europe's elite club competition.
Ronald Araujo also opened his Liverpool account, while Jeremie Frimpong headed home and Lewis Koumas scored after twice being denied by the offside flag as Andoni Iraola's side responded emphatically to Sunday's 3-0 Premier League defeat by Manchester City.
That match was City's first since being found guilty of 114 breaches of financial rules and they host two-time defending champions Paris St Germain later on Wednesday.
Barcola's hat-trick offered some welcome relief after a slow start to his Liverpool career, with the French forward facing growing scrutiny following his big-money move.
Iraola will be less satisfied with Liverpool's defensive display after Florian Flecker struck twice in three second-half minutes and Robert Ljubicic also scored for LASK.
Liverpool began their campaign with a 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid, while LASK suffered a narrow 1-0 defeat by AEK Athens in their opener in September.

items.title: Houthis bring the war to Riyadh
items.author: Andrew Mills
items.creator: Andrew Mills
items.summary: The Houthis say they are not finished. On Wednesday, the Iran-backed group promised to keep hitting Saudi airports and oil facilities and told civilians, workers and "international shipping companies" to leave them. The same day, loud booms were heard over Riyadh, and the Saudi-led coalition said it had shot down a ballistic missile aimed at the capital. The threat came a day after a strike on Saudi Aramco's headquarters in Dhahran. The energy ministry called it a limited fire, but sources told Reuters that the blaze spread across several floors. Aramco staff are now working from home.
items.body:
The Houthis say they are not finished. On Wednesday, the Iran-backed group [USN:L6N4600LI TEXT:"promised to keep hitting"] Saudi airports and oil facilities and told civilians, workers and "international shipping companies" to leave them. The same day, loud booms were heard over Riyadh, and the Saudi-led coalition said it had shot down a ballistic missile aimed at the capital. The threat came a day after a strike on Saudi Aramco's headquarters in Dhahran. The energy ministry called it a limited fire, but sources told Reuters that the blaze spread across several floors. Aramco staff are now working from home.
[USN:L8N460160 TEXT:"Pilgrims"] have been caught up in the attacks too. Footage of Saturday's blast at Riyadh airport showed many travelers in the white cloth ihram clothes worn on the journey to Mecca. Saudi media reported that a Bangladeshi imam leading a group of pilgrims was among the dead. The Houthis have promised to spare Mecca and Medina. Still, people at the Grand Mosque say the constant phone alerts make them anxious.
Can Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's plan to remake the economy survive a war on his doorstep? Our analysis looks at how the kingdom got here, and the tough questions it now faces. Plus: why Saudi Arabia's missile alerts went quiet before the deadliest strike. And in our news briefing: Iran's new campaign against shipping, Yemen's overwhelmed hospitals and "Davos in the desert" going hybrid.
NEWS BRIEFING Iran has shifted tactics to [USN:L8N45Z15J TEXT:"step up attacks on shipping"] in and beyond the Strait of Hormuz, aiming to keep oil prices high and sway the US midterms, two senior Iranian officials told Reuters. Attacks have surged to their highest since the war began, deepening risks to global energy supplies.
Hospitals across Yemen are [USN:L6N4600LK TEXT:"overwhelmed by soaring war casualties"], and intensified fighting has cut off aid to around 800,000 people, relief agencies said. The renewed Houthi-government war, reignited by the US-Iran confrontation, has left the encircled city of Taiz short of food and medicine, prompting warnings of a humanitarian catastrophe.
Saudi Arabia plans to make its flagship Future Investment Initiative conference this month a [USN:L6N45Z0WN TEXT:"hybrid event"], letting executives attend remotely after deadly attacks on Riyadh airport, sources said. The shift highlights how the escalating war with the Houthis is challenging the kingdom's push to attract investment and become a global events hub.
ANALYSIS: AFTER A WEEK OF HOUTHI STRIKES, SAUDI ARABIA FACES TOUGH QUESTIONS Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis have brought the war to the heart of Saudi Arabia
in the past week, repeatedly striking Riyadh's international airport and, on Tuesday night, hitting the headquarters of Saudi Aramco, the world's largest oil and gas company and the backbone of the Saudi economy.
Saturday's strike on the airport killed at least 13 people and wounded more than 300, the deadliest attack in the kingdom in more than a decade.
The barrage is testing Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's bet that he can overhaul the kingdom's economy while staying out of the region's wars.
But the crisis did not come out of nowhere. It grew, in part, from an unfinished war in Yemen, a US security umbrella that keeps failing to open and an economic plan that the crown prince was already redrawing.
The crown prince's Vision 2030 made big bets on costly, futuristic giga-projects meant to wean the kingdom's economy off oil. But by 2025, many of those projects were indefinitely on hold as the kingdom reworked its economic strategy.
When the United States and Israel launched their war on Iran in February, Riyadh initially appeared likely to escape the worst of it. Tehran's missiles and drones struck some Saudi targets, but the heaviest damage was in the UAE, Qatar, Bahrain and Kuwait.
With the Strait of Hormuz effectively shut, Aramco ran its East-West pipeline at its maximum capacity of 7 million barrels per day (bpd) and shipped exports out through the Red Sea. The company reported a 25% jump in first-quarter profit, the envy of producers in neighbouring Gulf states.
Aramco's oil kept flowing largely because the Houthis, Riyadh's foe on its southern border, did not formally join the war. The kingdom's tankers loaded at Red Sea ports and sailed unimpeded through the Bab el-Mandeb chokepoint to Asia.
But a truce between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition collapsed in early July. The group declared a naval blockade of Saudi Arabia, attacked Saudi vessels and the East-West pipeline and, most alarmingly, seized Yemen's Red Sea coastline and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
The crown prince then called President Donald Trump at least twice, seeking US military support to push back the group. He got intelligence and targeting support, not air strikes, in another reminder that the US security umbrella the kingdom had relied on for decades was no longer a sure bet.
Nevertheless, the Saudi-backed Yemeni government launched an offensive against the Houthis earlier this month that has made slow gains, while the Houthis besieged Taiz.
This week's strikes on the airport and Aramco's headquarters followed. The Houthis had declared such sites legitimate targets and, on Wednesday, called the attacks retaliation for Saudi strikes on Yemen.
Events are still moving too quickly to tell how, or whether, Riyadh can stay the course. Can oil keep flowing to its Asian customers while the Houthis control the Bab el-Mandeb? Will investors come when foreign direct investment last year reached only a third of the crown prince's $100 billion target? Can a state that relies on Aramco's dividends pay for a war and an economic overhaul at the same time? And will Trump, who has hinted that Washington "may" join Saudi strikes, finally step in?
CHART OF THE WEEK As Mohammed bin Salman tries to build the country's tourism profile and foreign countries issue travel advisories, Muslim pilgrims were still landing and flying out of Riyadh when [USN:S8N44G01P TEXT:"Houthis struck the capital's airport"]. The group has struck several other airports such as Dammam, Abha, Najran and Jazan. These attacks raised worries over civil aviation becoming a target in armed conflict.
"This level of sustained intense attack on civil aviation is unprecedented," said Mark Zee, founder of OPSGROUP, a membership-based organization that provides aviation safety advice.
"I think this requires us to rethink how we view the current risk picture, and tread very carefully," he said.
Air traffic tracker Flightradar24 showed planes avoiding the city on Monday, though jets were crossing Saudi airspace and landing at top hub Jeddah on the country's west coast. Cancellations across all Saudi airports reached 46.4%, aviation analytics firm Cirium said.
LAST WAVE: THE WARNINGS THAT NEVER CAME Saudi Arabia's [USN:L8N45X021 TEXT:"early warning system went silent"] even as Houthi attacks mounted. The kingdom's last public alert of an incoming attack went out on September 29, days before strikes on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport killed at least 13 people and wounded more than 300.
The government has not explained why. But when officials from an allied Western government asked, Saudi authorities said the alerts were too disruptive and that many citizens had complained of being woken by them at night, two officials told Reuters.
Even Western embassies, which send staff their own internal alerts, got no warning before Saturday's strike, the deadliest.
The silence ended on Monday when civil defense issued new alerts for Riyadh and southern cities. Former US ambassador Michael Ratney said the lack of warnings "creates the very nervousness they are trying to avoid."

Oct 14 : Iowa, Kansas and six other states said on Wednesday they had sued OpenAI in courts across the country over harms they say ChatGPT has caused to children, alleging the chatbot has coached children to harm themselves or others. 
The lawsuits, which were filed in state courts, are seeking an order forcing OpenAI to make changes to how ChatGPT works for children. The states are also seeking an order forcing the company to give up profits it has generated from young users.
Florida's attorney general was the first to sue OpenAI, bringing a lawsuit over similar claims in June. The company is also facing dozens of lawsuits alleging ChatGPT aided in mass shootings or other violence.

Source: Reuters

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [１４日　ロイター] -
items.body:
[１４日　ロイター] - 米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が１４日発表した地区連銀経済報告（ベージュブック）で、米国の労働市場は雇用も解雇も低水準にとどまる状態が続く一方、一部地域でインフレ圧力が強まっていることが示された。

地区連銀経済報告は「企業はディーゼル（軽油）価格の高止まりを報告し、燃料サーチャージを通じてコスト上昇がサプライチェーン全体に転嫁されていると指摘した」と報告。物価動向について、１２地区連銀のうち３地区で全般的な価格上昇が「力強い」と報告され、８地区は「緩やか」と報告された。

雇用については、大半の地区で全体的な雇用水準にほとんど、もしくは全く変化がみられなかったと報告した。

全般的な経済活動は、２地区で「緩やかな」ペースで成長。３地区は「控えめ」なペース、４地区は「小幅な」成長を報告し、３地区では経済活動に大きな変化は見られなかった。国内の多くの地域で企業が景気見通しについて前向きな見方を維持していると報告されたが、「成長見通しは概して小幅なものにとどまり、製造業がけん引する一方で、根強い不確実性が重しとなっている」とした。

今回の報告は１０月５日までに収集された情報に基づき、フィラデルフィア地区連銀が作成した。

items.title: Eight US states sue OpenAI, claiming ChatGPT harms children
items.author: Diana Jones
items.creator: Diana Jones
items.summary: Iowa, Kansas and six other states said on Wednesday they had sued OpenAI in courts across the country over harms they say ChatGPT has caused to children, alleging the chatbot has coached children to harm themselves or others.
items.body:
Iowa, Kansas and six other states said on Wednesday they had sued OpenAI in courts across the country over harms they say ChatGPT has caused to children, alleging the chatbot has coached children to harm themselves or others.
The lawsuits, which were filed in state courts, are seeking an order forcing OpenAI to make changes to how ChatGPT works for children. The states are also seeking an order forcing the company to give up profits it has generated from young users.
Florida's attorney general was the first to sue OpenAI, bringing [USN:L6N429106 TEXT:"a lawsuit"] over similar claims in June. The company is also facing dozens of lawsuits alleging ChatGPT aided in mass shootings or other violence.

items.title: Libro Beige de la Fed muestra presiones inflacionarias en un contexto de alza del combustible
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: El mercado laboral estadounidense se mantuvo en un estado de baja contratación y pocos despidos, pero la inflación se intensificó en varias partes del país en las últimas semanas, según un informe de la Reserva Federal del miércoles, que subraya lo que se juega este mes el banco central, que debe decidir si sube las tasas de interés por segunda reunión consecutiva.
items.body:
El mercado laboral estadounidense se mantuvo en un estado de baja contratación y pocos despidos, pero la inflación se intensificó en varias partes del país en las últimas semanas, según un informe de la Reserva Federal del miércoles, que subraya lo que se juega este mes el banco central, que debe decidir si sube las tasas de interés por segunda reunión consecutiva.
Si bien empresas en gran parte del país tienen una perspectiva económica positiva, sus "expectativas tienden a ser de un crecimiento leve, con mayor peso en la manufactura y lastradas por incertidumbres persistentes", dijo la Reserva Federal en su último "Libro Beige", un compendio de datos basados en encuestas y comentarios de empresas recopilados por sus 12 bancos regionales, que ofrece a los responsables de la política monetaria una visión de las condiciones económicas actuales.
"Las empresas informaron de altos precios del diésel y señalaron que los recargos por combustible estaban trasladando el aumento de los costos a de toda la cadena de suministro", dice el informe, que señala que tres de los 12 distritos de la Reserva Federal describieron el crecimiento de los precios como sólido y ocho como moderado, mientras que tres señalaron que se estaba "intensificando".
"Los contactos en varios distritos también mencionaron la continua presión sobre los precios derivada de otras materias primas, los aranceles y los seguros", añade el informe.
La encuesta también sirve como una especie de barómetro de las presiones económicas a las que se enfrentan los votantes estadounidenses antes de las elecciones legislativas del 3 de noviembre, que determinarán si el Partido Republicano del presidente Donald Trump mantiene el control del Congreso.
El costo de la vida es el principal asunto que mencionan los votantes en una reciente encuesta de Reuters/Ipsos.
El mes pasado, la Reserva Federal aumentó su tasa de interés oficial un cuarto de punto porcentual, situándola en el rango del 3,75% al 4, 00%, y la mayoría de los responsables de la política monetaria de los bancos centrales han indicado que probablemente será necesario otro aumento de las tasas este año, aunque probablemente no hasta diciembre.
Sin embargo, los mercados financieros ahora dan prácticamente las mismas probabilidades de una subida de tasas en la reunión de la Reserva Federal del 27 y 28 de octubre, después de que datos publicados el miércoles mostraron que los precios al consumidor aumentaron un 3,7% en los 12 meses a septiembre, mucho más rápido que el objetivo del 2% del banco central y más que el pronóstico consensuado de los economistas encuestados por Reuters.
El aumento del precio de la gasolina, derivado del conflicto de siete meses en Oriente Medio, fue en gran parte responsable del incremento del IPC, si bien el rápido aumento de los precios del software y los juguetes también apunta al impacto de la demanda impulsada por la inteligencia artificial y a los aranceles más elevados impuestos por la política comercial de la administración Trump.
El creciente costo de los préstamos para comprar una vivienda representa una carga adicional para muchos hogares estadounidenses. La tasa promedio de una hipoteca a tasa fija a 30 años subió la semana pasada al 7,5%, el nivel más alto en casi tres años, según informó el miércoles la Asociación de Banqueros Hipotecarios.
Los datos para el último Libro Beige de la Reserva Federal se recopilaron el 5 de octubre o antes.

items.title: Pope Leo back on his feet after shock cancer diagnosis
items.author: CNA
items.summary: The diagnosis has raised concerns about the 71-year-old pontiff’s health and the future of his papacy, though the Vatican says his recovery is progressing well.
items.body:

Pope Leo back on his feet after shock cancer diagnosis

The diagnosis has raised concerns about the 71-year-old pontiff’s health and the future of his papacy, though the Vatican says his recovery is progressing well.

Pope Leo arrives at Gemelli Hospital ahead of the pontiff's surgery to remove a lung nodule, in Rome, Italy, Oct 13, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Guglielmo Mangiapane)

15 Oct 2026 02:42AM

VATICAN CITY: Pope Leo 's recovery from surgery is progressing as expected and he has begun walking in his hospital room and eating normally, the Vatican said on Wednesday (Oct 14), after doctors announced the 71-year-old pontiff was being treated for lung cancer .
World leaders, Catholics across the globe and senior cardinals at the Vatican have offered prayers for Leo after he had part of his right lung removed in an operation on Tuesday.
Blood tests and a chest X-ray carried out on Wednesday showed normal post-operative results, the Vatican said, adding that the pontiff had undergone respiratory physiotherapy.
The cancer diagnosis for a pope known to be relatively young and energetic and who was elected only in May 2025 caused shock and raised questions about the future shape of his papacy as he deals with the illness.

Leo normally follows a very busy schedule. He is due to make a tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from Nov 6 to 17 and the Vatican press office said on Wednesday that "nothing has changed" regarding the planned trip.
However, Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori said on Wednesday that the dates could change because of the amount of time his recovery would take.
The pope is the ultimate earthly authority for the world 's 1.4 billion Catholics and does not have a deputy who steps in when he is sick. When a pope is incapacitated, the business of the Vatican's vast bureaucracy carries on as usual, holding off on any decisions that require papal approval.

PRAYERS FOR LEO A prayer was recited for Leo to have a good convalescence and complete healing during an open-air Mass in St. Peter's Square on Wednesday following the surgery.
The pope has been diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma, the most common form of lung cancer , and doctors removed the lower lobe of his right lung during Tuesday's operation in an effort to eliminate all cancer ous tissue.
Human lung s have five lobes - three in the right lung and two in the left.
The operation lasted about 90 minutes and was completed without complications, the pope 's lead surgeon, Professor Stefano Margaritora, and his personal physician, Dr. Luigi Carbone, said late on Tuesday.
The Vatican has not disclosed the size of the tumour or whether the disease had spread to nearby lymph nodes, key factors in determining prognosis.
Dr. Serena Ricciardi, a lung cancer specialist at Rome's San Camillo Forlanini Hospital, said that if the cancer had not spread to Leo 's lymph nodes, the surgery may have been sufficient for treatment.
"If there are no further issues or lymph node involvement, we could consider the surgery curative," she told Reuters. "The disease has been completely removed."
Leo is relatively young for a Church leader. He enjoys sports, including tennis, and is not known to be a smoker or to have had recent health issues.

Related:

What we know about Pope Leo's lung cancer diagnosis

Pope Leo recovering after lung cancer operation

ENGAGEMENTS CANCELLED UNTIL NEXT WEEK The Vatican said this week that the pope was expected to remain in hospital for about a week and that all his public engagements had been cancelled until Oct 20.
The Mass on Wednesday was the closing act of an assembly of bishops called by Leo to discuss the Church's family life teachings, the largest gathering of Church leaders so far during this papacy.
Filipino Cardinal Luis Tagle led the service in place of Leo . The pope last week approved Tagle as the dean of the Church's College of Cardinals, in the first selection of an Asian cleric to the elite role.
Political leaders offered messages of support.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he and his wife Jeanette were praying for the pope , an American who was born in Chicago.
"May the Lord give him strength and the Holy Spirit guide the medical professionals taking care of the Holy Father," he said on X. Rubio met Leo at the Vatican in May.
There was no immediate response on social media from US President Donald Trump, who has criticised the pope , or from Vice President JD Vance, who is a Catholic.

Source: Reuters/fs

items.title: Pesquisa do Fed mostra pressões de preços ganhando força em meio a alta de custos dos combustíveis
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: O mercado de trabalho dos EUA permaneceu estagnado em um cenário de poucas contratações e demissões em massa, enquanto a inflação se intensificava em várias regiões do país nas últimas semanas, segundo relatório divulgado na quarta-feira pelo Federal Reserve, ressaltando o que está em jogo enquanto o banco central avalia se deve realizar um segundo aumento consecutivo da taxa de juros ainda neste mês.
items.body:
O mercado de trabalho dos EUA permaneceu estagnado em um cenário de poucas contratações e demissões em massa, enquanto a inflação se intensificava em várias regiões do país nas últimas semanas, segundo relatório divulgado na quarta-feira pelo Federal Reserve, ressaltando o que está em jogo enquanto o banco central avalia se deve realizar um segundo aumento consecutivo da taxa de juros ainda neste mês.
Embora as empresas em grande parte do país tenham uma perspectiva positiva, suas “expectativas tendem a ser de um crescimento moderado, com ênfase no setor manufatureiro e prejudicadas por incertezas persistentes”, afirmou o Fed em seu mais recente relatório “Livro Bege”, um compêndio de dados baseados em pesquisas e comentários de empresas compilados por seus 12 bancos regionais para fornecer uma visão das condições econômicas.
“As empresas relataram preços elevados do diesel e observaram que as sobretaxas de combustível estavam repassando os custos aumentados por toda a cadeia de suprimentos”, afirmou o relatório. Ele observou que 3 dos 12 distritos do Fed descreveram o aumento dos preços como robusto e 8 como moderado, com 3 deles observando que ele estava “se intensificando”.
“Contatos em vários distritos também observaram pressão contínua sobre os preços proveniente de outras commodities, tarifas e seguros”, afirmou o relatório.
A pesquisa também funciona como uma espécie de barômetro das pressões econômicas que os eleitores estão enfrentando antes das eleições de meio de mandato de 3 de novembro, que determinarão se o Partido Republicano do presidente Donald Trump manterá o controle do Congresso.
O custo de vida é a principal questão citada pelos eleitores em uma pesquisa recente da Reuters/Ipsos.
O Fed aumentou sua taxa básica de juros em 0,25 ponto percentual, para a faixa de 3,75% a 4,00%, no mês passado, e a maioria dos formuladores de política monetária indicou que provavelmente será necessário outro aumento este ano, embora provavelmente não antes de dezembro.
Os mercados financeiros estão precificando uma probabilidade de cerca de 37% de um aumento dos juros na reunião do Fed de 27 a 28 de outubro, depois que dados divulgados nesta quarta-feira mostraram que os preços ao consumidor (CPI, na sigla em inglês) subiram 3,7% nos 12 meses até setembro, muito mais do que a meta de 2% do banco central e acima da previsão consensual dos economistas consultados pela Reuters.
O aumento nos custos da gasolina devido à guerra no Oriente Médio foi o principal responsável pelo aumento do CPI, com os preços em rápida elevação de softwares e brinquedos também apontando para o impacto da demanda impulsionada pela IA e das tarifas mais altas sob a política comercial de Trump.
O aumento do custo dos empréstimos para a compra de imóveis é um fardo adicional para muitas famílias americanas. A taxa média das hipotecas de taxa fixa de 30 anos subiu na semana passada para 7,5%, o nível mais alto em quase três anos, informou a Associação dos Bancos Hipotecários na quarta-feira.
Os dados para o último “Livro Bege” foram coletados até 5 de outubro.
(Reportagem de Ann Saphir)

items.title: BofA Takes US Regulatory Fines Seriously, CEO Moynihan Says
items.summary: Bank of America Corp. Chief Executive Officer Brian Moynihan addresses the $1.2 billion in fines levied against the company by the US government. He says the bank takes the fines seriously and there is accountability at the firm. He says costs associated with these fines are in the company "baseline." He speaks to Bloomberg's Jonathan Ferro. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Panamá pone en marcha dos fideicomisos para la ayuda humanitaria y la reconstrucción tras el sismo
items.author: Fátima Romero
items.summary: Los dos fideicomisos, uno manejado por el Estado y otro con gobernanza de la empresa privada, se destinarán para asistir a las personas afectadas, así como para la reparación, rehabilitación y constru ...
items.body: Bloomberg Línea — El Gobierno de Panamá anunció los mecanismos financieros para reconstruir las provincias centrales golpeadas por el sismo de magnitud 7,5 del viernes 9 de octubre, que dejó 11.460 personas afectadas, 1.250 viviendas con daños y 27 heridos leves, sin fallecidos ni desaparecidos, según el balance oficial. Ver más: Panamá declara estado de emergencia nacional y habilita hasta US$100 millones tras el terremoto El Centro de Operaciones de Emergencia (COE) del Sistema Nacional de Protección Civil (Sinaproc) reportó además 3.667 familias damnificadas y 2.840 personas que permanecen en albergues. Más de 600 centros educativos y 90 edificios gubernamentales presentan daños, mientras continúan las inspecciones de las autoridades en Coclé, Herrera, Veraguas y Los Santos. Para financiar la recuperación, el ministro de Economía y Finanzas, Felipe Chapman, detalló que el país contará con dos fideicomisos separados. El primero operará en el Banco Nacional de Panamá y canalizará los recursos no reembolsables del Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo, la CAF, el Banco Mundial, el Banco Centroamericano de Integración Económica (BCIE) y el Fondo Monetario Internacional, además del cobro de pólizas de seguros catastróficos. El segundo se constituyó en la Caja de Ahorros para recibir aportes del sector privado, en dinero y materiales, destinados a las familias que perdieron sus hogares. “No se van a mezclar recursos”, subrayó Chapman, quien anunció que un portal web de acceso público permitirá auditar cada desembolso en tiempo real, bajo supervisión de la Contraloría General de la República. Esta estructura evitaría que el Ejecutivo solicite a la Asamblea Nacional una dispensa de la Ley de Responsabilidad Fiscal, por lo que el país mantendrá su meta de déficit de 3,5% del producto interno bruto. Chapman descartó recurrir al Fondo de Ahorro de Panamá, pues su ley exige daños superiores al 0,5% del PIB, unos US$450 millones, umbral que la emergencia no alcanzaría según estimaciones preliminares. El Consejo de Gabinete autorizó hasta US$100 millones mediante la declaratoria de estado de emergencia nacional del 10 de octubre. “Estamos todavía muy lejos de llegar a los 100 millones”, precisó el ministro, quien anticipó que solo se usarían líneas de crédito contingentes si las donaciones resultaran insuficientes. Mientras el marco financiero toma forma, este miércoles los ministros de Educación, Salud, Vivienda, Desarrollo Social y Obras Públicas recorren las zonas afectadas para evaluar daños y coordinar la asistencia, bajo la dirección del presidente José Raúl Mulino. El Ministerio de Vivienda y Ordenamiento Territorial inició el traslado de materiales de construcción desde sus bodegas de la capital y de Santiago de Veraguas, y la comisión de crisis ofrecerá informes diarios desde Azuero. En el terreno, Sinaproc mantiene más de 500 personas desplegadas entre voluntarios y colaboradores. El Ministerio de Salud, con 66 de sus 842 instalaciones dañadas, ha atendido a más de 6.000 pacientes, recibió 16 carpas de Unicef que operarán como hospitales de campaña y dispuso la licitación del nuevo hospital de Tonosí, valorado en unos US$30 millones. Las autoridades han movilizado más de 121.000 libras de ayuda por vía aérea y unas 331 toneladas de agua para comunidades y hospitales. El estadio Roberto “Flaco Bala” Hernández, en Las Tablas, funciona como principal centro de acopio y distribución de la ayuda humanitaria. El sismo también golpeó el patrimonio de La Villa de Los Santos, fundada en 1569 y escenario del primer grito de independencia de 1821. Allí se derrumbó parcialmente el campanario de la iglesia de San Atanasio, símbolo del pueblo, y los vecinos recogieron de entre los escombros las conchas que lo decoraban con la esperanza de devolverlas a su sitio, según reportó Efe . Por lo pronto, el Gobierno advirtió que las cifras continuarán actualizándose conforme avancen las evaluaciones y exhortó a la población a consultar fuentes oficiales y evitar difundir información no verificada. El Ministerio de Vivienda habilitó en la página web miviot.gob.pa un formulario para que los afectados puedan reportar los daños en sus viviendas.

items.title: Red hot CPI report fuels AI rout
items.author: Chuck Mikolajczak, Darshan R, Shashwat Chauhan
items.creator: Chuck Mikolajczak, Darshan R, Shashwat Chauhan
items.summary: Major AI stocks slumped on Wednesday following the latest hot US inflation report, highlighting investor concern about the risks posed by rising borrowing costs in this capital-intensive sector.
items.body:
Major AI stocks slumped on Wednesday following the latest [USN:L6N4600XF TEXT:"hot US inflation report"], highlighting investor concern about the risks posed by rising borrowing costs in this capital-intensive sector.
Among the [USN:L4N4601KQ TEXT:"leading decliners"] were data center operator CoreWeave (CRWV.O) , which fell 16%, AI infrastructure provider Nebius (NBIS.O) , off 11%, cloud computing giant Oracle (ORCL.N) , down 9%, and AI server seller Dell Technologies (DELL.N) , down 11%. Together the declines erased some $80 billion of market value.
The declines reflect the impact of tightening financial conditions, as well as the outsize gains scored by some of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom. Barclays on Wednesday downgraded Dell and two other enterprise hardware stocks, noting that Dell shares have quadrupled this year — part of an AI-fueled investor binge that has resulted in 16 stocks in the S&P 500 technology sector (.SPLRCT) at least doubling this year, according to Reuters calculations.
Concern over rising borrowing costs also weighed on Wednesday's other big decliners. Selling has been particularly intense in CoreWeave, which has issued $22 billion of bonds and $26 billion of loans, according to LSEG data. A CoreWeave bond that was issued in June yielding 9.625% recently yielded 15%.
"We're getting a whole lot of information suggesting that the largest AI companies may not be generating the earnings or revenue people anticipated, and I think that makes everyone nervous about companies like CoreWeave," said Kim Forrest, chief investment officer at Bokeh Capital Partners.
Coreweave Chief Executive Officer Mike Intrator said in an internal memo the market is acting “irrationally” and that he remains confident in the AI cloud company, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday.
Wednesday's rout is the latest sign of a market struggling to come to grips with the implications of high inflation at a time when AI-fueled corporate borrowing has helped push up global interest rates.
Investors generally remain sanguine on the sector in part because its largest players, from chip maker Nvidia (NVDA.O) to the so-called [USN:L4N45T0NO TEXT:"hyperscalers"] — primarily Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , Microsoft (MSFT.O) , Meta (META.O) and Amazon (AMZN.O) — are highly profitable and widely perceived as well managed, despite concerns about debt.
But higher rates will make borrowing and building costlier, a fact that is likely to hit unprofitable and less-profitable firms first. On Wednesday, US interest rates rose following the hot inflation report, pushing the 30-year yield as high as 5.63% before rates pulled back sharply in the afternoon.
"I do think long rates above 5% and creeping towards 6% is a problem for the marginal borrower, I'll call them," said Ross Mayfield, investment strategy analyst at Baird, in an interview with Reuters. "It gets a lot harder for the tiers below the kind of big four hyperscalers."
The Nasdaq (.IXIC) was down 2% on Wednesday afternoon, with Alphabet and the other major hyperscalers mostly down between around 2%. SpaceX (SPCX.O) , another major AI player, was down 3%.
"I guess it's grown to a group of five now. SpaceX has kind of joined the party here to join in with like Meta and Microsoft and Google and Amazon," said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management. "Those five are spending like 75% of the money that's being invested in data centers here in the country. And those five are obviously putting all their profits and then some into these data centers and the returns they're generating from those are really good."
Despite the strong economics of these firms and their investments, Ellerbroek said it's not surprising that investors remain skeptical about the AI buildout, in part because of the busts that have preceded this one, particularly the dot-com meltdown that started in 2000.
"This select group of companies is driving most of the growth in the economy and the stock market, and they're investing so, so aggressively and investors just aren't really willing to pay for it or fully buy in to the extent that we saw in the late 90s or whatever when investors kind of lost their minds," Ellerbroek said. "Investors have definitely not lost their minds. They're being very cautious and I think selective."

items.title: Zelenskiy recebe apoio total do Reino Unido depois que Trump se voltou contra ele
items.author: William James
items.creator: William James
items.summary: Volodymyr Zelenskiy recebeu uma forte demonstração de apoio em Londres nesta quarta-feira, ao se reunir com o primeiro-ministro britânico, Andy Burnham, e o rei Charles, depois que as relações do líder ucraniano com os Estados Unidos sofreram uma brusca deterioração.
items.body:
Volodymyr Zelenskiy recebeu uma forte demonstração de apoio em Londres nesta quarta-feira, ao se reunir com o primeiro-ministro britânico, Andy Burnham, e o rei Charles, depois que as relações do líder ucraniano com os Estados Unidos sofreram uma brusca deterioração.
Zelenskiy foi recebido com todas as honras, chegando ao Reino Unido após mais uma noite de intensos ataques russos e poucas horas depois de a Ucrânia acusar a SpaceX, de Elon Musk, de incapacitar seus drones ao limitar os serviços da Starlink.
A demonstração diplomática, que incluiu uma audiência de 25 minutos com Charles e uma guarda de honra em Downing Street, ecoou a visita de Zelenskiy a Londres em fevereiro de 2025, logo após ele ter entrado em conflito com o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, e seu vice, JD Vance.
No início da reunião desta quarta-feira em Downing Street, Zelenskiy disse que queria discutir as dificuldades relacionadas à Starlink e ao compartilhamento de informações de inteligência, e que a Ucrânia ainda contava com sua parceria com os Estados Unidos.
Trump afirmou no fim de semana que Zelenskiy deveria ser substituído como líder da Ucrânia, dias depois de ter fechado um acordo com Moscou para suspender as sanções às exportações russas de diesel.
O Reino Unido afirmou que não apoia o acordo entre os EUA e a Rússia sobre o diesel e pediu que os aliados mantenham a pressão econômica sobre Moscou.
Em entrevista ao jornalista Piers Morgan, Zelenskiy disse que foi doloroso ver Trump tomar o partido da Rússia em detrimento da Ucrânia.
Burnham disse que os últimos dias foram “muito sombrios e difíceis” para a Ucrânia, mas que o Reino Unido continuava sendo um aliado firme. “Estamos ao seu lado, e isso não vai mudar”, afirmou.
Anteriormente, ele anunciou a entrega planejada de 45 milhões de libras (US$59,60 milhões) em mísseis terra-ar usados para atingir drones russos movidos a jato, com 10 milhões de libras desse pacote sendo liberados em regime de urgência para atender a uma necessidade imediata na Ucrânia.
Burnham solicitou que as autoridades elaborassem novas sanções e ajuda militar, e seus ministros das Relações Exteriores e da Fazenda têm pressionado os aliados a seguirem o exemplo do Reino Unido na proibição de serviços marítimos que apoiem as exportações russas de gás natural liquefeito.

items.title: Illinois QB Katin Houser (hand) out 4-6 weeks
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Illinois quarterback Katin Houser underwent a medical procedure on his right (throwing) hand and is expected to be sidelined for four to six weeks, head coach Bret Bielema announced Wednesday.
items.body:
Illinois quarterback Katin Houser underwent a medical procedure on his right (throwing) hand and is expected to be sidelined for four to six weeks, head coach Bret Bielema announced Wednesday.
Houser sustained the injury while attempting to make a tackle on an interception return in the third quarter of Saturday's 38-37 overtime victory at Michigan State.
Michael Clayton II replaced Houser and tossed a 25-yard touchdown pass to Hudson Clement on the first play of overtime in East Lansing, Mich.
Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns for Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten), which returns to action on Oct. 24 against Oregon in Champaign, Ill.
"I had a long conversation with him Sunday night kind of about what it means to be a starting quarterback in this league and in college football," Bielema said of Clayton on Wednesday. "... Excited about his opportunity."
Houser, a transfer from East Carolina who began his college career with Michigan State, has completed 66.3% of his passes for 1,440 yards with 12 touchdowns and four interceptions in six games this season. He also has rushed for 120 yards and two TDs.
--Field Level Media
