items.title: US Transportation Secretary meeting with Boeing, GE CEOs on aircraft certification reform efforts
items.author: David Shepardson
items.creator: David Shepardson
items.summary: US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy on Wednesday is meeting with the CEOs of major aerospace companies including Boeing and GE on his efforts to reform new aircraft certification, officials said.
items.body:
US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy on Wednesday is meeting with the CEOs of major aerospace companies including Boeing (BA.N) and GE (GE.N) on his efforts to reform new aircraft certification, officials said.
On Sept. 30, Duffy said he wants to speed certification of new airplanes from Boeing and other manufacturers, citing competition concerns from China. Approving a new airplane can take five or more years and require substantial testing and data and extensive documentation. The Federal Aviation Administration in June proposed changes to modernize and speed certification of new commercial airplanes.
A spokesperson for Duffy confirmed he was meeting with industry executives. Boeing and GE declined to comment.
"If we can't move at a different pace in certification, we're going to lose. China is going to beat us. We're going to lose not because you don't have the innovation," Duffy told reporters last month, warning that private capital is not going to invest in innovation because it is going to take a decade for approvals.
The effort could be a boost to manufacturers like Boeing (BA.N) Airbus (AIR.PA) Embraer (EMBJ3.SA) and Bombardier (BBDb.TO) .
It took Boeing over eight years to get the smaller 737 MAX 7 certified, which was finally approved in August. The certification of the 777x is more than five years behind Boeing's original schedule.
FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford has pushed for reforms to certification and disclosed earlier this year the agency has a few projects working with industry "to see how they can streamline the process."
The prior FAA head, Mike Whitaker, told Reuters in 2024 that the agency was looking at using better technology to streamline the process.
Reuters first reported the FAA's planned changes in September, disclosing the agency planned to reduce the number of "exemptions, special conditions, and equivalent level of safety findings required during the certification process."
Duffy also urged more entrants in commercial space. "It needs to be more vibrant. We need more competition, more players," Duffy said, adding the government is also trying to move faster in space to speed innovation.

WASHINGTON: US consumer prices accele rate d in September as the cost of gasoline surged, dealing another blow to US President Donald Trump and his Republican Party ahead of the Nov 3 midterm elections and putting an interest rate increase later this month back on the radar.
The Consumer Price Index report from the Labor Department on Wednesday (Oct 14) showed a broadening of price pressures beyond energy, raising concerns among economists that underlying inflation could be getting sticky. Financial markets now see the Fed eral Reserve's interest rate decision this month as a closer call than before the data was released.
The report added to surveys this month that showed a further deterioration in consumer sentiment and a plunge in Trump's approval rating, driven by angst over the rising cost of living. A Reuters/Ipsos poll showed about 78 per cent of Americans blamed Trump's policies, including tariffs on imports and the Middle East conflict, for rising prices, which are outpacing wages.
"The last mile back to target could remain bumpy and keep interest rate s elevated," said Jeffrey Roach, chief economist at LPL Financial. "The report complicates the Fed 's decision this month , as the road back to price stability is looking increasingly difficult to navigate."

The CPI rose 0.6 per cent last month after climbing 0.4 per cent in Aug us t, the Labour Department's Bureau of Labour Statistics said. The increase in the CPI was in line with economists' expectations.
A 9.1 per cent surge in gasoline prices accounted for more than half of the increase in the CPI over the month . The US -Israeli war with Iran is driving up energy prices. Diesel prices have vaulted to record highs and there are fears that those costs will soon feed through to higher prices at the s up ermarket.
Food prices were unchanged after gaining 0.1 per cent in both July and Aug us t. Grocery store prices dipped 0.1 per cent over the month , but rose 1.8 per cent on a year-over-year basis. Beef prices dropped 1.0 per cent in September and the cost of dairy and related products eased 0.9 per cent. But prices for nonalcoholic beverages surged 0.9 per cent, while fruits and vege table s cost 0.5 per cent more.
In the 12 month s through September , the CPI advanced 3.7 per cent after rising 3.4 per cent in Aug us t.

CORE INFLATION ABOVE EXPECTATIONS Excluding the volatile food and energy components, the CPI gained 0.3 per cent in September , matching the gain in Aug us t. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the so-called core CPI would rise 0.2 per cent. The core CPI was lifted by a 0.4 per cent increase in the cost of shelter, including hotel and motel rooms. Owners' equivalent rent rose 0.3 per cent.
There were increases in the costs of recreation and education. Prices for us ed cars and trucks increased 0.7 per cent, while airline fares rose 1.2 per cent amid higher jet fuel prices. Apparel prices climbed 0.3 per cent.
In the 12 month s through September , core CPI inflation increased 2.6 per cent after advancing 2.4 per cent in Aug us t. The US central bank tracks the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index for its 2 per cent inflation target.
The core CPI measure is lagging core PCE inflation , which increased 3.0 per cent in Aug us t, beca us e of the different weights assigned to the components in the baskets.
Financial markets raised the chances of a rate hike at the Fed 's Oct 27-28 policy meeting to roughly 52 per cent from about 22 per cent prior to the CPI report, CME Gro up 's Fed Watch Tool showed. The odds of a rate increase this month had diminished following underwhelming payroll gains in September as well as cooler-than-expected PCE inflation readings for July and Aug us t.

Related:

Stocks fall, dollar rallies as US inflation tops forecasts

Egyptian foreign minister urges diplomacy, says ‘no military solution’ to Middle East conflict

US Treasury yields were mostly higher while the dollar advanced vers us a basket of currencies. US stocks opened lower.
The Fed in September raised its overnight benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to the 3.75 per cent-4.00 per cent range, its first hike in three years, and flagged further increases in borrowing costs in the month s ahead. Economists had expected the Fed to raise rate s in December.
The September CPI inflation report was keenly awaited by millions of retirees and other Social Security recipients trying to figure out how much their benefits will increase next year.
The Social Security Administration announced a 3.6 per cent cost-of-living adj us tment for Social Security and S up plemental Security Income benefits for 2027. The programmes benefit older Americans who have retired as well as the disabled and certain widows, widowers and children.

Source: Reuters/fs

items.title: US judiciary to weigh broadcasting federal trials for crime victims
items.author: Nate Raymond
items.creator: Nate Raymond
items.summary: A US judicial rulemaking panel is considering whether to create a narrow exception to the longstanding ban on TV and audio broadcasts of federal criminal trials to allow victims to watch the proceedings remotely.
items.body:
A US judicial rulemaking panel is considering whether to create a narrow exception to the longstanding ban on TV and audio broadcasts of federal criminal trials to allow victims to watch the proceedings remotely.
The proposal was discussed during a meeting in Boston of the US Judicial Conference's Advisory Committee on Criminal Rules, which only two years ago [USN:L1N3MD1SL TEXT:"voted against"] a request by media organizations to more broadly lift the ban against broadcasting federal criminal proceedings.
Most state courts already allow televised trials. Following the COVID-19 pandemic, federal courts have permitted remote audio access to proceedings in civil and bankruptcy cases when testimony is not being taken.
But the federal judiciary had held firm on the broadcasting ban in criminal cases, which dates back to 1946. Judges in 2024 cited concerns about how to protect the privacy of witnesses and jurors in deciding to maintain the bar on cameras.
Recently, though, Senior US District Judge Michael Mosman of Oregon, the committee's chair, appointed Debevoise & Plimpton partner [USN:KBN1392KR TEXT:"Mary Jo White"], the former chair of the US Securities and Exchange Commission, to head a subcommittee that would consider a narrow lifting of the ban.
Chicago-based US District Judge Edmond Chang last year suggested amending the rule to permit victims and third-party custodians at bail hearings to watch criminal case proceedings remotely.
Chang did so after finding that he was barred in one narcotics-related case from allowing the mother of a victim who died of an overdose to listen to a sentencing hearing via a closed-circuit feed from Arizona, where she lived, even though both the prosecution and defense supported giving her that option.
Congress has twice allowed such closed-circuit televising of criminal proceedings for victims' benefit, starting with the 9/11 Victims Access Act of 2002, which allowed them to watch the case against Zacarias Moussaoui, the only person ever convicted in a US court in connection with al Qaeda's September 11, 2001 attacks.
Congress later passed the Lockerbie Victims Access Act, which was enacted in 2024 and allows victims and family members to watch from afar the [USN:S0N43J05A TEXT:"criminal trial proceedings"] scheduled for next year in Washington, DC, of a former Libyan intelligence operative accused of building the bomb that brought down Pan Am Flight 103 over Lockerbie, Scotland, in 1988.
White said her panel plans to meet in November and would also look at whether family members of defendants should be given the ability to watch proceedings remotely as well.
The panel would also examine what restrictions would be imposed, such as if an out-of-state victim would need to watch any broadcast from within their local federal courthouse.
But White noted the limits of any exception her panel may ultimately recommend, noting that the two earlier laws gave judges the discretion to still bar broadcasting entirely "in order to protect the defendant's right to a fair trial."
Read more:
[USN:L1N3MD1SL TEXT:"Panel votes to maintain ban on cameras in US federal criminal trials"]
[USN:L1N3AO2H5 TEXT:"US federal courts to allow limited remote audio access post-pandemic"]
(This story has been refiled to specify federal trials in the headline.)
items.raw_description: A US judicial rulemaking panel is considering whether to create a narrow exception to the longstanding ban on TV and audio broadcasts of federal criminal trials to allow victims to watch the proceedings remotely.

items.title: Quênia confirma segundo caso de Ebola, um parente do primeiro paciente
items.author: Humphrey Malalo, Vincent Nzilani
items.creator: Humphrey Malalo, Vincent Nzilani
items.summary: O Quênia registrou um segundo caso de Ebola na quarta-feira, cerca de uma semana após registrar seu primeiro caso de infecção pela doença viral, quando um queniano que morava no Congo morreu em um hospital de Nairóbi no dia 5 de outubro.
items.body:
O Quênia registrou um segundo caso de Ebola na quarta-feira, cerca de uma semana após registrar seu primeiro caso de infecção pela doença viral, quando um queniano que morava no Congo morreu em um hospital de Nairóbi no dia 5 de outubro.
O segundo paciente, um homem de 39 anos, é parente próximo do primeiro caso e já estava em quarentena quando adoeceu na terça-feira, informou o Ministério da Saúde em comunicado. Segundo o comunicado, ele foi isolado imediatamente após apresentar sintomas, incluindo febre, fadiga e dores nas articulações.
“Ambos os casos estão relacionados, e não há evidências de disseminação na comunidade em geral”, afirmou o ministério.
O segundo caso, no entanto, aumentará as preocupações no Quênia, o quarto país a registrar um caso relacionado à epidemia de Ebola no Congo — a segunda maior já registrada globalmente, com mais de 9.000 casos e mais de 4.000 mortes.
O primeiro caso surgiu depois que um queniano, que havia adoecido no Congo cerca de um mês antes de viajar por estrada para Uganda, voou para Nairóbi em 3 de outubro, onde um parente o levou de carro ao hospital.
Esse caso gerou preocupações quanto a falhas nos sistemas de triagem nas fronteiras da região, já que o paciente conseguiu cruzar a fronteira entre o Congo e Uganda, que está fechada desde maio.
As autoridades quenianas localizaram 113 dos 128 contatos do primeiro paciente, com 108 pessoas em quarentena.
“Os outros cinco estão fora do Quênia, e as autoridades de saúde desses países foram informadas... O rastreamento dos 15 restantes continua”, informou o ministério.
As autoridades também estão realizando avaliações de todas as pessoas que tiveram contato com o segundo paciente desde o surgimento de seus sintomas, incluindo profissionais de saúde e funcionários do centro de quarentena.
“Essa é a resposta funcionando conforme planejado”, acrescentou o ministério, informando que compartilhará atualizações sobre a evolução do paciente.
Ele pediu aos quenianos que mantenham a calma, mas permaneçam vigilantes.
O Ebola se espalha por contato direto com fluidos corporais de pessoas infectadas, vivas ou mortas. A doença pode causar febre, vômito, diarreia e, em casos graves, hemorragias internas e externas.

items.title: Airbus terá em breve decisão sobre aumento de produção de jato A350
items.author: Tim Hepher
items.creator: Tim Hepher
items.summary: A Airbus planeja decidir “o mais rápido possível” sobre o aumento da capacidade de produção de seu jato de fuselagem larga A350, afirmou o presidente-executivo da divisão de aviação comercial do grupo, Lars Wagner.
items.body:
A Airbus (AIR.PA) planeja decidir “o mais rápido possível” sobre o aumento da capacidade de produção de seu jato de fuselagem larga A350, afirmou o presidente-executivo da divisão de aviação comercial do grupo, Lars Wagner.
A maior fabricante de aeronaves do mundo também está estudando ativamente versões maiores do A350 e do modelo menor, o A220, que vem gerando prejuízos, com decisões sobre ambos os projetos previstas para o início de um período de planejamento de cinco anos, disse ele.
“A decisão de aumentar a taxa de produção do A350 é inevitável. Vamos fazê-lo porque o mercado claramente exige mais aeronaves”, disse Wagner a jornalistas.
“É uma grande decisão, por isso precisamos levá-la ao conselho de administração. Mas isso vai acontecer mais cedo ou mais tarde.”
A Airbus possui uma linha de montagem para o concorrente das séries 787 e 777 da Boeing, projetada para produzir de 12 a 13 jatos por mês. Aumentar essa produção exigirá uma nova linha e um novo sistema industrial, disse Wagner.
Separadamente, o executivo disse que há “claramente demanda” por um A350 mais longo e com mais assentos, amplamente conhecido como A350-2000, e por uma versão maior do A220, de aproximadamente 130 assentos, conhecido como A220-500.
O ex-presidente-executivo da MTU Aero Engines, que assumiu o comando da maior divisão da Airbus este ano, se recusou a dizer se a Airbus poderá abrir mão da posição de ter a Rolls-Royce (RR.L) como única fabricante de motores do A350 quando se trata de equipar a nova versão.
Fontes do setor afirmam que a Airbus cogitou a possibilidade de usar um motor da GE Aerospace para o A350-2000, com cerca de 400 assentos, mas que o interesse da fabricante de motores tem sido discreto até o momento.
Wagner reiterou que a Airbus está confiante em atingir as metas de entrega até o final do ano, apesar das recentes falhas de qualidade.
A longo prazo, a Airbus continua considerando a data “teórica” de 2030 para o lançamento de um jato de corredor único totalmente novo, disse Wagner.
O momento do lançamento dos sucessores das séries mais vendidas, o Boeing 737 e o Airbus A320, é uma das decisões mais aguardadas do setor, impulsionada em parte pelas pesquisas das empresas de motores.
Alguns analistas estão céticos quanto à possibilidade da próxima geração de jatos tomar forma já em 2030, à medida que os fabricantes de motores aperfeiçoam tecnologias avançadas. O presidente-executivo da Boeing (BA.N) , Kelly Ortberg, disse à Aviation Week em julho que a próxima geração está “avançando na direção certa”.
MOTORES PRATT & WHITNEY No curto prazo, a Airbus afirmou que continua enfrentando incertezas quanto ao fornecimento de motores Pratt & Whitney para os jatos da família A320.
A Airbus e a subsidiária da RTX (RTX.N) vêm debatendo quem terá acesso prioritário ao fornecimento de motores, as fábricas de aeronaves ou as oficinas de reparo das companhias aéreas.
A Airbus afirmou que ainda não chegou a um acordo com a Pratt sobre o fornecimento após 2026.
“Estamos lidando com isso com muita seriedade junto à Pratt & Whitney e tentando avançar o máximo possível”, disse Florent Massou dit Labaquere, chefe de operações da Airbus.
O número de aeronaves em serviço imobilizadas devido a atrasos no fornecimento de motores de reserva é “ainda bastante significativo”, acrescentou ele.
A Reuters informou em março que a Airbus havia dado o pontapé inicial em uma ação por indenização por atrasos na entrega de motores, em uma disputa que pode chegar a bilhões de dólares.
As negociações entre as duas empresas para evitar uma batalha judicial ainda não resultaram em avanços significativos, segundo fontes do setor.
A Airbus acusou a Pratt de voltar atrás quanto ao número de motores alocados às suas fábricas. A Pratt, que fornece cerca de 40% dos jatos A320, informou que houve progresso na estabilização dos suprimentos.
“A Pratt & Whitney aumentou as entregas anuais de novos motores desde 2019, superando o setor e nossa participação geral no mercado para a frota”, afirmou a RTX em comunicado enviado por email, acrescentando que continua a expandir a capacidade de manutenção.
Massou disse, no entanto, que as interrupções no fornecimento de um modelo diferente de motor da Pratt para o A220 praticamente desapareceram. Os motores da Rolls-Royce também estão em dia após preocupações anteriores, mas os atrasos no fornecimento de assentos continuam sendo uma questão urgente para os jatos de fuselagem larga, acrescentou ele.

items.title: Federal judge blocks planned US farm agency reorganization
items.author: Leah Douglas
items.creator: Leah Douglas
items.summary: A federal judge on Tuesday blocked the US Department of Agriculture from proceeding with its planned agency reorganization, in a blow to President Donald Trump's sweeping overhaul of the executive branch.
items.body:
A federal judge on Tuesday blocked the US Department of Agriculture from proceeding with its planned agency reorganization, in a blow to President Donald Trump's sweeping overhaul of the executive branch.
The ruling from the District Court for the Northern District of California is a victory for unions that had [USN:L1N44T0OQ TEXT:"sued"] to block the reorganization effort, in part because employees said it would [USN:L6N43T0ZQ TEXT:"weaken"] agency services.
The order halts reorganization efforts at several USDA agencies, including the Agricultural Research Service, Forest Service, Food and Nutrition Administration, and others.
Judge Vince Chhabria said the agency was "reprogramming" congressional funds for the reorganization, or using money for a different purpose than it was intended.
"Congress did not contemplate USDA using its appropriated funds to shut down offices or relocate employees," Chhabria wrote.
The agency's [USN:L6N41613W TEXT:"reorganization "]effort has sought to move about 2,600 employees from the Washington region, as well as to consolidate agency offices across the country.
Agency staff had [USN:L6N43T0ZQ TEXT:"warned"] that wide-scale employee departures because of the reorganization risked trade, foreign aid, nutrition and other programs.
A USDA spokesperson said, “The Department is reviewing the Judge’s decision and will file its response with the Court."
"The administration’s attempt to gut this essential agency is blatantly illegal, and we’re thankful the court has stopped it, for now, from proceeding with a reckless plan," said Patrick Moran, president of the American Federation of State, County & Municipal Employees, in a statement.

items.title: Los incendios en la Amazonía brasileña aumentan avivados por El Niño y el cambio climático
items.author: Bruno Kelly
items.creator: Bruno Kelly
items.summary: El Niño, el cambio climático y la actividad humana están provocando este mes un aumento de los incendios en el corazón de la Amazonía brasileña, mientras los bomberos se apresuran a contener las llamas, cuyo humo está asfixiando a los residentes y provocando la cancelación de eventos en las localidades cercanas.
items.body:
El Niño, el cambio climático y la actividad humana están provocando este mes un aumento de los incendios en el corazón de la Amazonía brasileña, mientras los bomberos se apresuran a contener las llamas, cuyo humo está asfixiando a los residentes y provocando la cancelación de eventos en las localidades cercanas.
En las dos primeras semanas de octubre hubo 1.679 incendios en el estado brasileño de Amazonas, lo que supone un aumento del 253% en comparación con el mismo periodo del año pasado, según datos del sistema de vigilancia de la Amazonía del país.
Los incendios, que las autoridades sospechan que fueron provocados, han llenado el cielo de columnas de humo y han provocado la declaración del estado de emergencia en al menos 36 municipios de Amazonas, causando problemas respiratorios a los residentes.
"Nuestra situación aquí es crítica", dijo Luiz Rios, un agricultor jubilado del municipio de Autazes, en el estado de Amazonas, que ha tenido dificultades para respirar por las noches, lo que le ha provocado hinchazón en la cara.
La mala calidad del aire provocada por los incendios ha obligado a cancelar eventos al aire libre en Manaos, la capital del estado con más de dos millones de habitantes, donde las escuelas públicas cerraron el miércoles.
Agosto y septiembre suelen ser el punto álgido de la estación seca en la Amazonía, cuando los incendios se vuelven más difíciles de controlar, antes del inicio de la temporada de lluvias, que suele traer alivio en octubre.
Este año, sin embargo, las lluvias han tardado. Científicos y autoridades señalan el fenómeno de El Niño, que se prevé que sea el más intenso jamás registrado, y el cambio climático como factores determinantes del aumento de los incendios.
"El estrés hídrico y el estrés térmico están azotando con extrema intensidad, creando una situación potencialmente peligrosa que, agravada por la actividad humana, amenaza esta biodiversidad, la salud de las personas y la productividad de estas tierras", dijo Carlos Durigan, geógrafo e investigador del Instituto de Investigación Ambiental de la Amazonía.

items.title: Ações europeias têm leve alta após resultados sólidos da ASML e ganhos no setor de saúde
items.author: Avinash P, Niket Nishant
items.creator: Avinash P, Niket Nishant
items.summary: As ações europeias registraram ganhos modestos nesta quarta-feira, depois que resultados financeiros sólidos da ASML tranquilizaram investidores preocupados com a demanda por IA, enquanto as ações do setor de saúde atingiram seu maior nível em mais de cinco semanas.
items.body:
As ações europeias registraram ganhos modestos nesta quarta-feira, depois que resultados financeiros sólidos da ASML tranquilizaram investidores preocupados com a demanda por IA, enquanto as ações do setor de saúde atingiram seu maior nível em mais de cinco semanas.
O índice pan-europeu STOXX 600 (.STOXX) subiu 0,43%, para 637,75 pontos. O índice do setor de saúde (.SXDP) foi o que mais se valorizou no índice de referência, subindo 2,3% e atingindo seu maior nível desde 7 de setembro.
Além disso, as ações da ASML (ASML.AS) subiram 1,2% após a empresa informar que os clientes já estavam buscando fazer pedidos de suas ferramentas avançadas de fabricação de chips para 2029 e 2030, o que demonstra que a demanda continua sólida.
“A ASML ajudou a sustentar o argumento otimista de que as ações do setor de tecnologia continuam apresentando bom desempenho, a demanda por chips permanece forte e os gastos com infraestrutura provavelmente continuarão até bem depois de 2027”, disse Gordon Kerr, estrategista macroeuropeu da KBRA.
Abalados por semanas de preços elevados do petróleo e rendimentos dos títulos públicos, os investidores europeus depositam suas esperanças nos lucros corporativos para dar um novo fôlego ao mercado de ações.
Mas os resultados têm sido irregulares até o momento. No início desta semana, a LVMH (LVMH.PA) , referência no setor de luxo, divulgou vendas no terceiro trimestre abaixo do esperado, à medida que uma acentuada deterioração no ânimo dos consumidores chineses afetou a demanda por suas marcas principais.
“Esperamos uma verdadeira dicotomia nos lucros”, disse Michael Field, estrategista-chefe de mercado de ações para a região EMEA da Morningstar, acrescentando que as empresas expostas a preços mais altos de energia e ao fraco ânimo do consumidor podem enfrentar dificuldades.
As ações do setor de mineração (.SXPP) lideraram as perdas setoriais nesta quarta-feira, com a Fresnillo sendo a que mais ficou para trás, após uma queda de 4,6% quando o JPMorgan reduziu seu preço-alvo para a ação.

items.title: Arturo’s proyecta triplicar sus restaurantes en Venezuela y prepara inversiones millonarias para 2027
items.author: Raylí Luján
items.summary: La cadena venezolana de comida rápida, que cumple 40 años, prevé pasar de 81 puntos de venta a entre 200 y 220 en el país en los próximos cinco a diez años.
items.body: Bloomberg Línea — Arturo’s quiere convertir cuatro décadas de presencia en Venezuela en el punto de partida de una nueva etapa de crecimiento. La cadena de comida rápida, especializada en pollo frito, prevé triplicar su red de restaurantes en el país durante los próximos cinco a diez años, una expansión que exigirá inversiones de decenas de millones de dólares y una renovación de buena parte de sus locales. La compañía, que actualmente opera unos 81 puntos de venta, está preparando su plan de inversión para 2027, con dos prioridades: abrir nuevos restaurantes y modernizar los existentes. La cifra definitiva todavía no está cerrada, pero la magnitud del proyecto ya anticipa el esfuerzo financiero que requerirá su estrategia. Ver más: Bolsa de Valores de Caracas fue notificada sobre negociación para compra de Arturo’s “Definitivamente, la cifra está en los millones de dólares”, dijo Javier Rodríguez, vicepresidente de Innovación durante una presentación con motivo del aniversario en Caracas. Al incluir el objetivo de triplicar la presencia nacional, agregó, la inversión se sitúa en las decenas de millones de dólares. La empresa espera presentar un plan formal con el monto definitivo entre finales de 2026 y comienzos de 2027. El anuncio llega después de una transformación iniciada en 2023, cuando Protinal Proagro adquirió la cadena y la incorporó a un grupo empresarial con presencia en distintos segmentos del negocio alimentario. La operación, que no tuvo un precio público divulgado, sumó a la estructura del grupo una red de restaurantes que entonces contaba con alrededor de 75 establecimientos, según informó Bloomberg Línea en agosto de ese año. La adquisición abrió la posibilidad de integrar más estrechamente la producción de alimentos con la venta directa al consumidor, en un momento en que Arturo’s necesitaba recuperar competitividad frente a sus rivales. Entre los problemas que la nueva administración identificó estaban una estructura de precios que había perdido atractivo y una propuesta comercial que requería adaptarse a los cambios en los hábitos de consumo. Desde entonces, la compañía ha orientado su estrategia a recuperar la frecuencia de visita, ampliar el público al que llega y actualizar una marca que durante años mantuvo prácticamente intacta su identidad visual y su oferta tradicional. Uno de los primeros cambios fue revisar los precios. La empresa sostiene que mantiene desde agosto de 2023 los precios de varios de sus productos en niveles competitivos y que no ha aplicado aumentos a esa oferta desde entonces. Entre sus apuestas estuvo la hamburguesa Panachrunch, lanzada en febrero de 2024 con un precio de US$2,99, una propuesta que buscaba atraer a consumidores que no necesariamente tenían al pollo frito con hueso entre sus primeras opciones de comida rápida. El producto se estrenó inicialmente en tres restaurantes y, según la compañía, generó una respuesta favorable desde su lanzamiento. Después llegaron nuevas opciones, como las alitas y los tenders de pollo, con los que Arturo’s amplió su menú para responder a preferencias de consumo distintas de las que habían definido históricamente a la marca. La diversificación también ha incluido pruebas regionales, como una oferta de chicharrones de pollo en el estado Lara, donde la empresa busca ganar terreno en un mercado en el que reconoce que no siempre ha sido la primera opción de los consumidores. La estrategia supone un cambio relevante para una cadena cuyo principal activo ha sido durante décadas la asociación con una receta y una experiencia reconocibles para el consumidor venezolano. Pero ampliar el menú también introduce una exigencia operativa: mantener la calidad y la consistencia de los productos mientras crece la complejidad de las cocinas. La propia dirección reconoce que ese objetivo todavía no está plenamente alcanzado. La compañía ha avanzado con rapidez en la incorporación de productos y en la recuperación de su actividad comercial, pero considera que debe mejorar la estandarización de sus restaurantes antes de acelerar el crecimiento a mayor escala. Esa es una de las razones por las que las remodelaciones ocuparán un lugar central en el plan de 2027. Arturo’s calcula que todavía tiene entre 60 y 65 puntos de venta por renovar, con inversiones distintas según el formato del establecimiento: locales independientes, restaurantes integrados en otras estructuras comerciales y espacios en ferias de comida. Durante 2026, la empresa ya ha iniciado trabajos en varios establecimientos y prevé abrir dos nuevos locales, además de otros tres antes de terminar el año, según lo anunciado en la presentación. También ha remodelado restaurantes en centros comerciales como Sambil Maracaibo, Sambil Valencia y Sambil La Candelaria, y trabaja en otros puntos de su red. Los cambios van más allá de la apariencia. Incluyen nuevas fachadas, iluminación, mobiliario, equipamiento y una distribución que busca mejorar tanto la experiencia del cliente como la eficiencia de las cocinas. La compañía también está incorporando cajas de autopago en establecimientos de alto volumen, aunque descarta convertir la automatización en el eje de su modelo: su apuesta es combinar la rapidez del servicio con el contacto humano que considera parte de la experiencia de marca. La renovación física tiene además una dimensión comercial. Según la empresa, los restaurantes remodelados han registrado resultados positivos durante los primeros meses posteriores a su actualización, aunque no divulgó cifras de ventas, tráfico o rentabilidad que permitan medir el impacto con precisión. Arturo’s nació en 1986, fundada por el empresario J. Arturo Gutiérrez, y construyó su presencia nacional alrededor del pollo frito y de una propuesta familiar de comida rápida. La cadena llegó a operar más de un centenar de restaurantes, antes de reducir su red durante los años de dificultades económicas y cambios en el consumo venezolano. Su adquisición por Protinal Proagro en 2023 marcó un punto de inflexión. El grupo, vinculado a la producción de alimentos y a marcas como Protinal, Proagro y Del Corral, incorporó así un canal de venta directa al consumidor a sus operaciones. La integración también ofrecía una oportunidad para aprovechar capacidades existentes en la cadena alimentaria, aunque la compañía no ha detallado públicamente cuánto ha reducido sus costes desde la compra. La recuperación de Arturo’s se produce en un entorno en el que el precio sigue siendo una variable decisiva para los consumidores. Aunque el mercado venezolano ha mostrado señales de recuperación en algunas actividades comerciales, la capacidad de compra continúa bajo presión por la inflación y la evolución de los ingresos. En ese contexto, mantener una oferta de precio accesible puede ayudar a impulsar las visitas, pero también obliga a controlar los costes de producción, distribución y operación. Para Arturo’s, el reto consiste en sostener esa competitividad sin sacrificar la calidad ni la rentabilidad de una red que aspira a crecer de forma significativa. El crecimiento fuera de Venezuela sigue formando parte de los planes de Arturo’s, pero no es la prioridad inmediata. La empresa había considerado entrar en mercados como Estados Unidos, México y Brasil, aunque decidió poner esos proyectos en pausa en 2024 para concentrar recursos en la recuperación de su red local. La dirección sostiene que salir al exterior antes de haber modernizado los restaurantes en Venezuela habría supuesto asumir nuevas inversiones sin haber consolidado todavía la experiencia que quiere ofrecer bajo la marca. La compañía no descarta retomar esos planes en el futuro, con Centroamérica y otros mercados latinoamericanos también entre las posibilidades. Ver más: Un día con un repartidor en Venezuela: Entre costos y ganancias Por ahora, la prioridad es ampliar la presencia nacional y mejorar la operación de los locales actuales. Pasar de 81 restaurantes a entre 200 y 220 implicaría añadir más de un centenar de puntos de venta, además de renovar decenas de establecimientos que ya están en funcionamiento. El ritmo de esa expansión dependerá del plan de inversión que la empresa termine de definir y de su capacidad para financiar y ejecutar las aperturas. A los 40 años, Arturo’s apuesta por una combinación de precios competitivos, innovación en el menú y renovación de sus restaurantes para recuperar terreno en el mercado venezolano. La prueba será convertir esa recuperación en un crecimiento sostenido, sin perder la consistencia operativa que la propia compañía identifica como una de sus principales tareas pendientes.

items.title: Ecuador se prepara para los meses más duros de El Niño: Noboa anuncia mantenimiento de la red eléctrica
items.author: Carlos Cuevas
items.summary: El presidente ecuatoriano prevé que el periodo más crítico del fenómeno climático se extienda desde finales de noviembre hasta febrero y anunció inversiones en las redes eléctricas.
items.body: Bloomberg Línea — El presidente de Ecuador, Daniel Noboa, afirmó este miércoles que el país se prepara para los meses más críticos del fenómeno de El Niño, cuyo impacto podría intensificarse desde finales de 2026 y extenderse hasta el primer trimestre de 2027. “Estamos preparándonos para los peores meses de El Niño, que van a ser desde finales de noviembre hasta febrero”, sostuvo Noboa en entrevista con Radio Centro de Ambato. Ver más: Esta es una de las claves del éxito para el 58% de las empresas ecuatorianas El mandatario puso como ejemplo las recientes granizadas e inundaciones en Quito para subrayar la necesidad de realizar mantenimiento a las redes eléctricas. “Hemos visto la cantidad de granizo que cayó en Quito, cómo se ha inundado, la cantidad de agua que ha habido en nuestros barrios”, declaró en la entrevista. El fenómeno de El Niño puede provocar lluvias intensas en algunas zonas de Ecuador y sequías en otras. Por eso, el Gobierno busca preparar la infraestructura eléctrica para responder a distintos escenarios climáticos. “Vamos a hacer mantenimiento e inversión en nuestra red de transmisión y en las distribuidoras”, agregó Noboa. Dos años atrás, Ecuador padeció apagones de hasta 12 horas diarias en medio de una crisis eléctrica relacionada, en cierta medida, con el estiaje. Y ahora, con la posibilidad de que el fenómeno de El Niño se agudice, hay quienes se preguntan si pasará lo mismo. En ese contexto, Noboa brindó un parte de seguridad recientemente, solo que en diálogo con Centro Digital: “Ninguna familia ecuatoriana va a tener algún corte de luz. No va a haber cortes”. Latinoamérica y el Caribe es una de las regiones más expuestas al fenómeno de El Niño, según un informe publicado por el Banco Mundial el 6 de octubre. Dentro de la región, Ecuador, Paraguay y Argentina figuran entre los países que podrían enfrentar los mayores efectos. “El Niño plantea riesgos adicionales a la baja, ya que las sequías en algunas partes de la región y las inundaciones en otras podrían afectar la producción y aumentar las presiones sobre los precios, con Ecuador, Paraguay y Argentina potencialmente enfrentando los mayores impactos” , dice al Banco Mundial. La vulnerabilidad regional responde, en parte, a la dependencia de la energía hidroeléctrica, que representa casi el 50% de la generación eléctrica. En países como Colombia y Ecuador, esa proporción alcanza el 70%. “Los episodios históricos, como los graves eventos de 1997-98 y 2015-16, indican que los déficits hidrológicos locales pueden reducir significativamente la producción hidroeléctrica, lo que obligaría a los sistemas eléctricos a sustituir rápidamente la energía limpia faltante con la costosa generación térmica dependiente de combustibles fósiles importados”, analiza el Banco Mundial. El Banco Central del Ecuador (BCE) estimó que los efectos de El Niño sobre la economía del país podrían sentirse con mayor fuerza en 2027 que en 2026, debido a sus posibles repercusiones en la producción, las exportaciones y los precios. “Un evento moderado podría reducir el crecimiento económico de 2027 en 0,5%, mientras que un evento fuerte podría restar 1,4%”, estimó el BCE. “Estos escenarios no constituyen una predicción sobre la ocurrencia o intensidad del fenómeno, sino un ejercicio técnico que permite estimar la sensibilidad de la economía ante distintos niveles de impacto climático”. Citando estudios regionales, la Cepal advirtió recientemente que un escenario extremo de El Niño, o Súper El Niño, reduciría la tasa de crecimiento del PIB real en Ecuador en 4,1%, es decir, más que lo proyectado por el BCE. Ver más: Ecuador declara inocentes a 32 tripulantes de barcos atacados por EE.UU. en el Pacífico

items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: O presidente da Ucrânia, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, disse em entrevista nesta quarta-feira que foi "doloroso" ver Donald Trump tomar outro lado na guerra em curso entre Ucrânia e Rússia, depois que o presidente dos EUA afirmou que Zelenskiy deveria ser substituído.
items.body:
O presidente da Ucrânia, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, disse em entrevista nesta quarta-feira que foi "doloroso" ver Donald Trump tomar outro lado na guerra em curso entre Ucrânia e Rússia, depois que o presidente dos EUA afirmou que Zelenskiy deveria ser substituído.
Zelenskiy disse ao programa “Piers Morgan Uncensored”: “É doloroso quando o presidente Trump escolhe um lado, que não é o nosso.”
Ele também disse que não se importava que Trump ficasse no meio entre a Ucrânia e a Rússia, mas acrescentou: “Se você está no meio, precisa permanecer no meio.”
Questionado se se sentia traído por Trump, que no fim de semana pediu que a Ucrânia elegesse um novo presidente após ter concordado em suspender as sanções às exportações russas de diesel, Zelenskiy respondeu: “Na verdade, sim... mas é um pouco mais complicado do que apenas minhas emoções ou meus sentimentos.”
“É uma pena estarmos perdendo um parceiro forte”, acrescentou.
Zelenskiy também disse: “Não estamos vendendo nosso país... para nós, não se trata de negócios, é simplesmente a nossa vida e este é o nosso país.”

WASHINGTON, Oct 14 : A group of Democratic lawmakers on Wednesday urged the Federal Aviation Administration to conduct a new environmental review before allowing an Amazon Prime Air drone delivery hub to be located about 30 miles (48.28 km) west of Boston.
Massachusetts Democratic US Senators Ed Markey and Elizabeth Warren and Representatives Jim McGovern and Lori Trahan wrote to FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford seeking a new review after communities raised concerns about the planned Westborough hub and its impact on the environment and residents’ quality of life, including noise pollution, health and safety, and privacy.
The FAA said it would respond directly to the lawmakers. Amazon did not immediately comment.

• On September 28, a group of 15 states and a Texas county on Monday sued the FAA over the agency's environmental review of planned commercial drone package delivery rules.
• The agency in July issued a broad environmental review that allows qualifying drone operators to launch fleets without a site-specific environmental analysis.
• The states — including New York, California, Massachusetts, Wisconsin and Michigan — and Harris County, Texas, said the FAA violated the law by failing to adequately analyze the potential environmental impacts of expanded drone package delivery operations.
• Drone delivery operations are already happening in states including California, Texas, Arkansas, Florida and Utah under the waiver process.
• The FAA said last year that eliminating the need for waivers "will significantly expand the use-case for drone technologies in areas like: manufacturing, farming, energy production, filmmaking, and the movement of products including lifesaving medications."

items.title: Las acciones europeas suben tras resultados de ASML y ganancias del sector de salud
items.author: Avinash P, Niket Nishant
items.creator: Avinash P, Niket Nishant
items.summary: Las acciones europeas cerraron al alza el miércoles, tras sólidos resultados de ASML que tranquilizaron a los inversores preocupados por la demanda de inteligencia artificial, mientras que los valores del sector sanitario alcanzaron un máximo de más de cinco semanas.
items.body:
Las acciones europeas cerraron al alza el miércoles, tras sólidos resultados de ASML que tranquilizaron a los inversores preocupados por la demanda de inteligencia artificial, mientras que los valores del sector sanitario alcanzaron un máximo de más de cinco semanas.
* El índice paneuropeo STOXX 600 (.STOXX) subió un 0,43%, a 637,75 puntos. El sector sanitario (.SXDP) lideró las alzas dentro del referencial, con una mejora del 2,3%, a un máximo desde el 7 de septiembre.
* Las acciones de ASML (ASML.AS) subieron un 1,2% después de que la empresa anunció que sus clientes ya estaban realizando pedidos de sus herramientas avanzadas de fabricación de chips para 2029 y 2030, lo que demuestra que la demanda sigue siendo sólida.
* "ASML ha contribuido a respaldar el argumento alcista de que las acciones tecnológicas siguen desempeñándose bien, la demanda de chips se mantiene fuerte y es probable que el gasto en infraestructuras continúe hasta bien entrado 2027", dijo Gordon Kerr, estratega macroeconómico para Europa de KBRA.
* Afectados por semanas de altos precios del petróleo y del rendimiento de la deuda pública, los inversores europeos han depositado sus esperanzas en los resultados empresariales para dar un nuevo impulso a la bolsa. Sin embargo, los resultados han sido desiguales hasta ahora.
* Más temprano en la semana, el referente del sector del lujo, LVMH (LVMH.PA) , comunicó unas ventas en el tercer trimestre inferiores a lo esperado, ya que el fuerte deterioro de la confianza de los consumidores chinos afectó a la demanda de sus marcas insignia.
* "Esperamos una verdadera dicotomía en los resultados", dijo Michael Field, de Morningstar, y añadió que las empresas expuestas a los precios más altos de la energía y a la debilidad de la confianza de los consumidores podrían tener dificultades.

items.title: Governo anuncia medidas de apoio a produtoras de videogames no Brasil
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: O governo federal anunciou nesta quarta-feira regulamentação de um conjunto de medidas de apoio para a produção de videogames no Brasil, que inclui R$200 milhões para serem destinados a financiamento do desenvolvimento de jogos e soluções digitais inovadoras por meio da Financiadora de Estudos e Projetos (Finep).
items.body:
O governo federal anunciou nesta quarta-feira regulamentação de um conjunto de medidas de apoio para a produção de videogames no Brasil, que inclui R$200 milhões para serem destinados a financiamento do desenvolvimento de jogos e soluções digitais inovadoras por meio da Financiadora de Estudos e Projetos (Finep).
O conjunto de medidas vem em um momento em que o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva disputa o segundo turno da eleição presidencial deste ano com o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), cujo pai, Jair, reduziu Imposto de Importação de videogames quando estava à frente do Palácio do Planalto.
As medidas anunciadas por Lula nesta quarta-feira também incluem facilitação do acesso de empresas brasileiras de games a crédito.
"Será proposta pela Agência Nacional do Cinema (Ancine) ao Comitê Gestor do Fundo Setorial do Audiovisual (FSA) a redução do valor mínimo dos empréstimos de R$500 mil para a faixa de R$150 mil", afirmou o governo em comunicado à imprensa.
A proposta também prevê reduzir os juros de TR mais 2% para TR mais 0,5% ao ano. Para 2026, o FSA prevê R$460 milhões em crédito para a indústria audiovisual, incluindo videogames.
O governo também anunciou a modalidade "Rouanet Games" voltado à captação de patrocínios pela Lei Rouanet, em parceria com empresas públicas.
O decreto reconhece que o setor de games pode acessar mecanismos federais de fomento de tecnologia, pesquisa, desenvolvimento, inovação e cultura e que caberá à Ancine regulamentar o acesso à Lei do Audiovisual e propor critérios de financiamento pelo FSA.

items.title: NWSL, USL to meet in new women's cup tournament
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The NWSL and the USL Super League will compete in a new women's cup competition, U.S. Soccer announced on Wednesday.
items.body:
The NWSL and the USL Super League will compete in a new women's cup competition, U.S. Soccer announced on Wednesday.
The Arthur M. Blank Crest Cup will feature a $1.7 million prize pool, with the winner earning a berth to the Concacaf W Champions Cup.
"Women's soccer continues to be one of the most dynamic and inspiring forces in sport," U.S. Soccer president Cindy Parlow Cone said in a statement. "The Crest Cup will create meaningful impact by bringing people together, attracting investment in the future of the game, and ensuring that excellence, inclusivity, and opportunity remain at the heart of women's soccer in the United States."
U.S. Soccer did not confirm a start date for the tournament. ESPN previously reported that it is expected to launch in 2028.
The single-elimination tournament will feature every team from NWSL (18 teams in 2028) and the USL Super League, which launched in 2024-25 and currently fields eight teams.
Blank, who contributed $50 million to build the new U.S. Soccer National Training Center near Atlanta, is the owner of the NFL's Atlanta Falcons, Atlanta United FC of MLS, Atlanta City FC of NWSL and the TGL squad Atlanta Drive GC.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr. (rib) likely to start Sunday
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. will likely start Sunday if there are no setbacks with his rib injury, head coach Kevin Stefanski said Wednesday.
items.body:
Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. will likely start Sunday if there are no setbacks with his rib injury, head coach Kevin Stefanski said Wednesday.
Penix is expected to practice on Wednesday as the Falcons (2-3) prepare for a home matchup against the Chicago Bears (3-2).
The Bears are not ruling out Caleb Williams playing for the first time since injuring his hamstring Week 2. Williams was limited in practice last Friday, two days before Chicago's loss at Green Bay, and did footwork and agility drills on the field before the game.
He's expected to increase activity following a walkthrough practice Wednesday and could play to push backup Tyson Bagent back to the bench.
Penix sustained the injury late in the fourth quarter of last Sunday's 30-23 overtime loss to the Baltimore Ravens after taking a hit to the ribs on a sack by Tavius Robinson.
Tua Tagovailoa replaced Penix in overtime and threw a game-ending interception on his second play.
Penix, 26, missed the first two weeks of this season to complete his recovery from ACL surgery. He has completed 67.5% of his passes for 719 yards, three touchdowns and one interception while posting a 2-1 record in three starts.
--Field Level Media

items.summary: The start time for Thursday's Game 3 of the American League Championship Series between the Tampa Bay Rays and Guardians has been moved up five hours due to forecasted rain in the Cleveland area.
items.body:
The start time for Thursday's Game 3 of the American League Championship Series between the Tampa Bay Rays and Guardians has been moved up five hours due to forecasted rain in the Cleveland area.
The game, initially scheduled to begin at 6 p.m. ET, will start at 1 p.m. ET, MLB announced Wednesday.
Right-hander Griffin Jax (0-0, 4.50 ERA) will start Game 3 for Tampa Bay. Cleveland has yet to announce its starting pitcher.
The Rays evened the best-of-seven series with the Guardians at 1-1 with a 3-1 victory on Tuesday in St. Petersburg, Fla. The Guardians recorded a 7-3 victory in the series opener on Monday.
--Field Level Media

items.title: México exige que plataformas digitais protejam menores de conteúdo violento e sexual
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: A presidente do México, Claudia Sheinbaum, afirmou que assinará, nesta quarta-feira, um decreto presidencial exigindo que as plataformas digitais, incluindo redes sociais e sites de streaming, protejam crianças e adolescentes de conteúdos violentos, sexuais e outros conteúdos prejudiciais.
items.body:
A presidente do México, Claudia Sheinbaum, afirmou que assinará, nesta quarta-feira, um decreto presidencial exigindo que as plataformas digitais, incluindo redes sociais e sites de streaming, protejam crianças e adolescentes de conteúdos violentos, sexuais e outros conteúdos prejudiciais.
O decreto, que intensificará a fiscalização das grandes empresas de tecnologia na segunda maior economia da América Latina, surge após um ataque perpetrado por dois ex-alunos de 18 anos a uma escola de ensino médio no Estado de Coahuila, no norte do país, no início de outubro, que deixou uma pessoa morta e outras três feridas.
As plataformas digitais terão um mês para se adequarem ao decreto, afirmou a assessora do governo Luisa Maria Alcalde.
Sheinbaum acrescentou que, caso as empresas não cumpram o decreto, o governo apoiará um projeto de lei para punir as plataformas.
Autoridades afirmaram que já se reuniram com representantes de Meta (META.O) , Microsoft (MSFT.O) , Apple (AAPL.O) , TikTok, Google (GOOGL.O) , X e Huawei para discutir o assunto. Essas empresas não responderam imediatamente aos pedidos de comentário.
A iniciativa do México segue uma tendência global mais ampla de proteção de menores na internet, com governos na Europa e na Austrália reforçando a fiscalização das plataformas digitais e Estados dos EUA adotando uma série de medidas de segurança infantil.
O Brasil também tomou medidas para fortalecer a proteção das crianças na internet. Tais medidas levantaram questões sobre como proteger menores ao mesmo tempo em que se salvaguarda a privacidade e a liberdade de expressão.

items.title: 米シティ、ＣＰＩ上振れでタカ派に転換　ＦＲＢの12月利上げ予想
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [１４日　ロイター] -
items.body:
[１４日　ロイター] - 米金融大手シティグループは１４日、９月の消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）が予想を上回ったことを受け、連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が１２月に政策金利を２５ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）引き上げるとの見通しを示した。

シティは、ＦＲＢが１２月に利上げを実施した後、金利を据え置くとの見方を示した。また、利下げ開始は２０２７年６月までないと予想している。金融市場で１２月の利上げ確率が約９４％に達する中、同行はこれまで唯一、年内の追加利上げはないとの見方を維持してきた。  

米労働省労働統計局が発表した９月のＣＰＩは前月比０．６％、前年比では３．７％上昇し、前月の０．４％と３．４％上昇から加速した。ガソリン価格の急騰を背景に伸びが加速した。

ＣＭＥのフェドウオッチによると、金利先物市場では、１０月２７─２８日に開かれる連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）での利上げ確率は４７．１％と、ＣＰＩ発表前の約２２％から上昇した。

items.body:
米シティ、ＣＰＩ上振れでタカ派に転換　ＦＲＢの12月利上げ予想
1:48 配信

米シティバンクのロゴ。2025年12月撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

[１４日　ロイター] - 米金融大手シティグループは１４日、９月の消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）が予想を上回ったことを受け、連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が１２月に政策金利を２５ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）引き上げるとの見通しを示した。

シティは、ＦＲＢが１２月に利上げを実施した後、金利を据え置くとの見方を示した。また、利下げ開始は２０２７年６月までないと予想している。金融市場で１２月の利上げ確率が約９４％に達する中、同行はこれまで唯一、年内の追加利上げはないとの見方を維持してきた。  

米労働省労働統計局が発表した９月のＣＰＩは前月比０．６％、前年比では３．７％上昇し、前月の０．４％と３．４％上昇から加速した。ガソリン価格の急騰を背景に伸びが加速した。

ＣＭＥのフェドウオッチによると、金利先物市場では、１０月２７─２８日に開かれる連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）での利上げ確率は４７．１％と、ＣＰＩ発表前の約２２％から上昇した。

items.title: As Wall Street banks finance and adopt AI, risks mount on both fronts
items.author: Manya Saini, Saeed Azhar, Tatiana Bautzer
items.creator: Manya Saini, Saeed Azhar, Tatiana Bautzer
items.summary: Wall Street's biggest banks want to ride the AI wave without getting caught in its undertow, as the promise of a lucrative infrastructure boom collides with questions over returns and new security threats.
items.body:
Wall Street's biggest banks want to ride the AI wave without getting caught in its undertow, as the promise of a lucrative infrastructure boom collides with questions over returns and new [USN:L4N4511UB TEXT:"security threats"].
Executives at the largest US banks this week discussed the risks of AI agents acting on customers' behalf and the uncertainty surrounding demand for the capital and computing power needed to fuel the technology's rapid growth.
"While we are proud of the privileged position we play in the AI investment cycle, no one knows how the demands for capital and compute will evolve as the broader AI ecosystem matures," Goldman (GS.N) CEO David Solomon said on a call with analysts.
"That will only become clearer as technology and markets continue to develop. This uncertainty reinforces the importance of remaining vigilant around the types of activity we finance and how we manage risk."
Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser does not believe that higher rates will slow down the investment in the AI infrastructure. "We're not seeing a slowdown in investment in the broader AI ecosystem. There's simply not enough compute," she said, referring to the processing power needed to develop and run AI models, supported by chips and data centers.
CAPITAL BEHIND THE GREAT AI BUILDOUT The scale of investment in AI infrastructure is [USN:S0N43A006 TEXT:"unprecedented"]. Big Tech has [USN:L4N41D03U TEXT:"committed billions"] to building data centers, the backbone of the computing capacity needed to train and run generative AI models.
For Wall Street, the buildout offers a chance to finance one of the biggest investment cycles in decades.
Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan said the enormous amount of AI capital investment is important for the lender's investment-grade debt and leveraged finance businesses.
Yet the financing opportunity hinges on several unknowns, from whether demand for computing power will keep pace with the industry's ambitious expansion plans to the returns data center projects can generate and the potential for local opposition.
"The AI investment cycle has become a complicated macroeconomic force in its own right," Wells Fargo CEO Charlie Scharf told analysts on a post-earnings call. He added that the buildout presents both opportunities and risks, given the significant leverage used to finance it and upward pressure on prices in some industries and supply chains.
"Having said this, the strength of the economy and the positive forces from these investments have thus far outweighed the potential downside," Scharf said.
Elevated interest rates that stay higher for longer, or rise further, could increase financing costs for data center projects, squeeze returns and make it more expensive for borrowers to service debt.
Morgan Stanley Chief Financial Officer Sharon Yeshaya said in an interview with Reuters that the bank was "very discerning" about the types of risks it was taking. "What you worry about is that peers and other firms allow for a loosening of credit standards, and that's kind of what creates the issue. We're very focused on making sure that we're not involved in those types of transactions." The bank's CEO Ted Pick told analysts the involvement in AI financing is "existential" for Morgan Stanley.
Investors, too, are weighing the economic benefits of the AI boom against the risk of losses on loans to projects that fail to deliver expected returns.
"To the extent that the tech spend is helping drive growth in the overall economy, that is a positive and material to the banks. If the credit exposure is directly related to certain projects like speculative data-center builds, it could lead to issues down the road," said Macrae Sykes, portfolio manager at Gabelli Funds, which holds several bank stocks.
Other investors say that banks are better positioned to manage those risks than some fear, having tightened their risk management practices after the financial crisis.
Dave Ellison, portfolio manager at Hennessy Funds, said banks have not abandoned the lessons of the crisis and are being more careful than investors fear. They are facilitating AI-related financing, but often as arrangers that distribute risk.
RINGFENCING EMERGING AI RISKS Beyond financing the buildout, banks are deploying AI in hopes of cutting costs and boosting productivity, but the financial payoff remains difficult to quantify.
"As important and dramatic and exciting as this theme is, it takes a long time to really do things that are visible at an institution of our size," JPMorgan CFO Jeremy Barnum said, adding that it is not a surprise that benefits are not yet observable in the bank's quarterly earnings.
Citi's Fraser said the bank is already seeing clear effects of the use of AI, such as developing products at lower cost and up to 40% faster. The use of coding tools has eased development and reduced tech vendor expenses by 30%, she said.
"We are seeing the financial benefits from AI and automation significantly outweigh the investments we've made year to date," Fraser said. The bank is using AI to reduce the volume of manual processes, as well as response time in client service.
Investors are betting on AI to deliver productivity gains across corporate America and valuations of US stocks leave little room for those gains to disappoint.
"If those gains in productivity and lower costs do not arrive by the end of next year, investors will begin to question the hype of AI," Brian Mulberry, chief market strategist at Zacks Investment Management, said.
At the same time, AI agents introduce new security challenges as they gain the ability to act autonomously. The technology is also adding to the threat posed by external cyber attackers.
JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon said that the lender is developing tools to navigate agentic AI risk.

Ukrainian drones hit Russia's top data centre in attack on AI ambitions

The attack follows a series of Ukrainian strikes on Russian data centres.

FAST

MOSCOW: Ukrainian drones hit Russia's biggest data centre on Wednesday (Oct 14), part of a series of attack s appearing to target Moscow's ambitions to develop Russian artificial intelligence capabilities on a par with those from the US and China.
The strike on the Balakovo data centre , owned by Sberbank, the country's largest bank and technology company, followed three attack s in the past week on data centre s owned by Russian technology group Yandex.
"We confirm that the data processing centre was attack ed. At the same time, all of Sberbank's systems and services are operating normally and without disruption," Sberbank First Deputy CEO Alexander Vedyakhin told reporters.
Russian President Vladimir Putin held a previously unannounced meeting on Wednesday with top officials on "information security", in which Sberbank CEO German Gref took part. The Kremlin s ai d that the meeting was not linked to the attack s on data centre s. Russia's state RIA Novosti news agency reported in 2024 that the Sberbank centre hit on Wednesday would host Russia's biggest supercomputer, which is scheduled to go into operation in 2027.

The Yandex data centre s, hit earlier, hosted all three of that company's operating supercomputers. Neither Yandex nor Sberbank has s ai d whether supercomputers, used to tr ai n the AI models, were damaged in the Ukrainian attack s.
Along with Yandex, its m ai n domestic rival, Sberbank is Russia's leading developer of artificial intelligence. The domestic market is shared between Sberbank's GigaChat model and YandexGPT.

DIFFICULTIES PURCHASING CHIPS Both companies have invested heavily in the development of their models but lag global leaders in the United States and China by up to nine months, according to Sberbank's own estimates, partly due to Western sanctions which hinder Russia's access to the most advanced hardware.
"It's clear what difficulties we face when purchasing modern graphics processing units. Both we and Yandex suffer from this," Gref s ai d on Sep 29, calling it the biggest reason why Russia lags behind the US and China in AI .
Sberbank is in talks to buy chips from Chinese makers, but in an interview with Reuters on Jun 3, Vedyakhin s ai d that US chipmaker Nvidia's NVDA.O monopoly on its CUDA software platform, which has become an AI industry standard, is an even greater problem.
Yandex s ai d previously that its supercomputers operated on Nvidia A100 chips, a model launched in 2020 and since then succeeded by more advanced H100 chips.
Sberbank has two functioning supercomputers. The most advanced one, called Christofari Neo, ranked 167th in the Top 500 list of the world's most powerful supercomputers, is located in Moscow and is based on Nvidia A100 chips.
Yandex's most advanced Chervonenkis supercomputer is ranked 101st in the same list.
IT expert Mikh ai l Klimarev told Reuters it could take a long time to replace the chips due to Western sanctions, while damage to the supercomputers could set back the Russian AI industry, which already suffered from sanctions.
"The equipment is being imported, but it's done at a high cost, through indirect routes. First, you need to negotiate so that someone is willing to sell it to you and is not afr ai d of sanctions," he s ai d.

PROTECT ASSETS Some commentators compared the lack of reported disruption at state-controlled Sberbank with Yandex - whose taxi and food delivery units had reported disruptions - saying it showed that Sberbank's centre s are better protected.
"This is a great example of what a business owner can do to protect their assets," wrote military blogger Alexander Kots. Under an August decree by Putin, the state can take over administration of poorly protected facilities.
The Sberbank site is located close to the Balakovo nuclear power plant, which the data centre uses as an energy source, and the Saratov hydroelectric power plant. No damage was reported to either plant from the attack .
Ukr ai ne says it is responding to Russian attack s on its own data sites. Both countries have attack ed each other's refineries, power stations, ports and e-commerce companies.
Russia's digital development ministry s ai d this week it was in talks with the military on protecting the data centre s, while some lawmakers called for them to be moved underground where the hardware will be out of reach for drones .
"We need a so-called Doomsday data vault," Valery Yermakov, deputy CEO of state-controlled Rostelecom, another major data centre operator, told a conference in Moscow.

items.title: Copper price forecasts lifted for 2026 but tariff “collapse” still on the table
items.author: Frik Els
items.creator: Frik Els
items.summary: Macquarie’s collapse scenario needs Washington to rule tariffs out, which it rates least likely. More likely is limbo past January 1, with 1.5 million tonnes of US copper staying exactly where it is.
items.body:
Copper price forecasts lifted for 2026 but tariff “collapse” still on the table

Staff Writer | October 14, 2026 | 9:31 am
Critical Minerals   Markets   China   Latin America   USA   Copper  

Where do we send these? Credit: Glencore

Copper pulled back from a three-week high on Wednesday after US inflation data put a Federal Reserve rate hike this month back on the table, and word of a preliminary deal to avert a strike at BHP’s Escondida, the world’s largest copper mine, took some of the supply premium out of the price.

Comex copper for December delivery traded at $6.6695 a pound (about $14,704 a tonne) late morning in New York, down 0.8%, after touching $6.7890 earlier in the session. The most-active contract’s record settlement of $6.89 was set on September 9 , the day before a report that the White House tariff plan had stalled knocked more than 5% off the price.

In London, three-month copper climbed as far as $14,700 a tonne, its highest since September 23, before easing to $14,532 by early afternoon. Cash copper settled at a record $14,822 on Monday and $14,741 on Tuesday, and LME inventories have fallen for seven straight sessions to 229,650 tonnes.

US consumer prices accelerated in September on a surge in gasoline costs, and the CME’s FedWatch tool put the odds of a quarter-point hike at the Fed’s late-October meeting at about 44%, double the day before, Reuters reported. New York Fed President John Williams said he still sees one more hike this year.

Two sources told Reuters that Escondida’s supervisors’ union and the company had reached a preliminary agreement , which members were voting on Wednesday morning, and a union leader told Bloomberg a deal was “virtually done”. Unions at Antofagasta’s Centinela returned to talks on Tuesday after a week-long stoppage, while the open pit at Codelco’s El Teniente remains shut after a deadly landslide .

Click on chart for live prices.

Copper’s 2026 advance has forecasters raising their numbers for the second time in three months, and with the metal averaging $13,471 a tonne for the year to date, the 2026 revisions mostly bring the sheet into line with the tape.

Macquarie now has copper averaging $13,573 this year, BMO Capital Markets $13,619 and BMI, a unit of Fitch Solutions, $13,500, up from the $12,700 it moved to in July . The differences open up from next year, and they come down to how much of the 1.5 to 2 million tonnes of copper now sitting in the United States is counted as surplus.

“The great copper gamble”

Macquarie, which in July called the rally “running ahead of reality” , has lifted its 2027 average by 14% to $12,750 and pushed the cycle low to $12,000 in the fourth quarter of next year from $11,000 a quarter earlier, while its long-term price rises to $10,500 a tonne in 2025 dollars.

Prices “have disconnected from the fundamentals and could arguably move higher or lower depending on the outcome of the Section 232,” the bank’s strategists write in a quarterly compendium whose copper chapter is headed “The great copper gamble”, listing the metal among its preferred commodities for the next six to nine months “but very binary”.

The fundamentals as Macquarie counts them are a 223,000-tonne surplus this year after a 531,000-tonne disruption allowance, and surpluses averaging more than 700,000 tonnes a year from 2027 as mine supply grows 4.9% next year and 4.3% in 2028, with Collahuasi, Grasberg, Kamoa-Kakula and Centinela ramping up, Tia Maria starting and Cobre Panama back in full from mid-2027.

Global demand growth slows to 1.5% in 2027 on its numbers, with none at all in China, where construction-related copper use is shrinking 9% a year and air conditioner makers are “again looking at aluminium substitution.”

Visible stocks worldwide are up 300,000 tonnes this year, but that is the US build; everywhere else they are down 168,000 tonnes, and Macquarie says sentiment will not turn until LME and Shanghai inventories start rising again, either quickly on a tariff decision or gradually as its forecast surpluses feed through.

Macquarie’s four tariff scenarios run from a January 1 that passes with no announcement at all, which it rates most likely, to a definitive decision against a duty, which it rates least likely: “the CME price will most likely collapse, taking the LME price with it, and the arb will invert,” with surplus US stocks reappearing in LME warehouses in the US and Asia.

A tariff announced six to eight weeks ahead of implementation would pull a last wave of metal into the US and leave the rest of the world “very tight”, while a formal six-month delay would see the spread fade as it did for platinum and palladium after the critical minerals decision.

Expectations are also growing that a scrap export ban will be folded into any decision; an immediate ban would take about 600,000 tonnes a year of contained copper off the world market.

“Has the market misread US inventory?”

BMO Capital Markets arrives at a very different place from a similar starting point. Its quarterly price deck, published two days before Macquarie’s, raises its long-term copper price by 47% to $16,000 a tonne in real terms, or $18,000 nominal by 2030, with $14,675 for 2027 and $16,000 for 2028, and the bank puts itself 46% above consensus on the long-term number. Its market balance is close to balanced throughout: an 83,000-tonne surplus this year, then small deficits from 2027.

The argument turns on what the US hoard, now close to 2 million tonnes on BMO’s estimate, or about a year of American consumption, actually represents. China’s refined copper imports have run below trend and its exports above trend since the tariff trade began, a cumulative swing of about 1.6 million tonnes on a net basis, which BMO reads as Beijing allowing its strategic reserve to run down while Washington built one.

“Instead of there being a build in above ground inventory over the last 2 years, there has been a geographical redistribution from ‘not visible’ to ‘visible’, meaning today’s price of ~$14,500-15,000/t is fundamentally supported,” the bank writes. Had China bid for metal alongside the US, “copper prices today would in fact be much, much higher,” and at some point China will want to restock.

BMO expects no tariff decision before the US midterms in November, which may see copper “pause for breath” and keep the Comex-LME spread narrow, but says investors it talks to are coming around to the view that the US stockpile “could simply stay in situ for many more years.”

Rising dependence on scrap, with China’s secondary refined output heading for 3.3 million tonnes this year from 2.8 million, is the other leg of its case: scrap is the marginal unit, and it only comes out at higher prices.

BMI sits between the two. It still views the rally “as having extended beyond what fundamentals alone would suggest” and has the market in a 43,000-tonne surplus this year, but has cut its 2026 mine supply growth forecast to 1.1% from 2.4% with Chilean output down 4%, and expects a deficit from 2027 that widens to 1.7 million tonnes by 2035 as demand grows 3% to 4% a year on grids, EVs and data centres.

Its 2027 forecast is $12,900, rising to $15,000 in 2029 and an unchanged $17,000 in 2035. The International Copper Study Group, meeting this week, lifted its 2026 surplus to 104,000 tonnes and kept 2027 at 368,000 tonnes.

The arb has gone, the metal has not

The spread that built the US stockpile has all but disappeared on a spot basis. Comex October copper at $6.62 a pound trades below LME cash, which at Tuesday’s $14,741 works out to $6.69, and John Gross of The Copper Journal calculates the month-to-date average has flipped to an 85-point LME premium from a 17-cent Comex premium in June.

Most of that is London’s doing: the backwardation that put cash $164.50 over three months at Monday’s settlement, since narrowed to $115.50, reflects how little spot metal is left outside the US.

Aurubis, Europe’s largest copper producer, has offered customers a record premium of $347 a tonne for 2027 supply, 10% above this year’s level, Benchmark Minerals reported, and a company spokesperson told Bloomberg that “a lot of material has relocated to the US, leaving warehouses quite empty.”

Further down the curve the premium survives. December Comex at $14,704 a tonne sits about $170 over LME three-month, which Macquarie read at the end of September as the market pricing a 10% chance of a 15% duty (on Wednesday’s prices the same arithmetic gives about 8%).

That is too little to pull fresh shipments across the Atlantic, but enough to keep what is already there in place as long as the Comex curve pays traders to hold it. The tonnes still arriving are cargo booked months ago: Comex stocks rose another 6,500 tonnes last week to 713,000 tonnes, with 100,000 tonnes of African and South American copper due through October.

Deutsche Bank takes the stockpiling argument furthest. Daniel Ghali, the bank’s new head of metals research, told the Wall Street Journal that with China adding to its strategic reserve for decades and the tariff threat pulling metal into American sheds, the two countries could be sitting on 71% of the world’s supply by the end of the year. On that trajectory copper “simply won’t be available” to users elsewhere by the end of 2028, an outcome averted only by prices high enough to force substitution into aluminium.

He sees $10 a pound, or $22,050 a tonne, in the second quarter of 2027, almost 50% above current levels. Even a decision against tariffs may not free the metal, he told the paper, since the LME has warehouses in the US and copper may simply be shuffled between American sites rather than leave the country.

Gross points to copper’s premium over aluminium, which hit a record $5.08 a pound in September, more than double its July 2022 low. “Clearly, this rising premium cannot continue indefinitely, but who among us will step forward to say it’s at the top?” he writes. His September monthly report makes the longer point: China consumed 58.9% of the world’s refined copper last year, up from 12.4% in 2000. “There are too many copper eggs in China’s basket.”

Miners still pricing $5 copper

Copper producers fell with the metal on Wednesday, Lundin Mining down 3.9%, Freeport-McMoRan 3.7%, Southern Copper 3.3% and Teck Resources 2.9%, but the year has been kind. Southern Copper is up 44.1% in 2026, taking its market value to $169 billion, with Glencore ahead 38.6%, BHP 38.0% and Freeport 37.4% at a $100 billion valuation. Teck has gained 36.1% and Anglo American 29.2%. Lundin has managed 13.0%, Antofagasta 7.5% with Centinela on strike, and First Quantum 3.0%.

RBC Capital Markets calculates that North American copper producers at 1.0 times net asset value imply a copper price of $5.03 a pound, from $5.98 for Freeport down to $3.96 for Ivanhoe Mines, against a futures price near $6.70. The group trades at 0.9 times net asset value, in line with its 10-year average.

Comex copper is up more than 18% in 2026.

items.author: Dawn C. Chmielewski
items.summary: La mayor parte de los recortes se producirán en los equipos de producto, tecnología, legal y recursos humanos, según se indicó.
items.body: Bloomberg — Netflix Inc. ( NFLX ) recortará el 6% de su plantilla global, lo que equivale a unos 1.000 puestos de trabajo, debido a la desaceleración del crecimiento de la compañía de streaming. La mayor parte de los recortes se producirán en los equipos de producto, tecnología, legal y recursos humanos, según escribieron los co-CEO Greg Peters y Ted Sarandos en un correo electrónico enviado a los empleados el miércoles, de acuerdo con una copia del memorando revisada por Bloomberg . Un representante de Netflix declinó hacer más comentarios. Ver más: Netflix obtiene los derechos exclusivos del Mundial de fútbol 2030 en España y Andorra “Decisiones como estas nunca son fáciles, y no las tomamos a la ligera”, escribieron los ejecutivos. El negocio de Netflix es “sólido y está en crecimiento, y seguimos encaminados a cumplir con nuestras previsiones para todo el año”, añadieron. Las acciones de Netflix bajaron menos del 1% el miércoles por la mañana en Nueva York. Han caído un 25% este año, en comparación con una ganancia del 13% para el S&P 500. Netflix. Símbolo: NFLX:UN. Clase de activo: equity. A principios de este año, Netflix fracasó en su intento por adquirir Warner Bros. Discovery Inc. ( WBD ). Los inversores interpretaron el intento de comprar el estudio de Hollywood y asegurarse su catálogo de personajes e historias ya consolidadas como una señal de debilidad subyacente. Wall Street ha perdido confianza en las acciones ante la creciente preocupación por el crecimiento y el debilitamiento de la captación de suscriptores. Los analistas también han expresado su preocupación por la falta de nuevos éxitos de taquilla en Netflix, lo que podría estar mermando la capacidad del servicio de streaming para retener a los espectadores. La interacción creció solo un 2% en el último período, y la compañía recibió la menor cantidad de premios Emmy en una década. Netflix ha estado buscando maneras de incentivar a sus 325 millones de suscriptores a pasar más tiempo en la plataforma y atraer más ingresos publicitarios, ante la desaceleración de su crecimiento. Mientras lucha por mantener a los espectadores enganchados a las series más allá de su primera temporada, Netflix se ha expandido al ámbito de los deportes y eventos en directo, los podcasts en video y la programación de algunos de los creadores más importantes de YouTube, intensificando así la competencia con el servicio de streaming propiedad de Google por el talento y la audiencia. Ver más: Netflix anuncia “La Gaviota”, la serie sobre Angélica Rivera: cuándo se estrena y quiénes la protagonizan En la reciente conferencia Bloomberg Screentime , Sarandos reconoció que Netflix no estaba creciendo tan rápido como él quería y dijo: “Estamos trabajando para acelerar ese crecimiento”. En el memorando, los ejecutivos afirmaron que Netflix continuará “invirtiendo de forma decidida en áreas de alto impacto para mejorar nuestro servicio e impulsar aún más el crecimiento y la innovación. Para ello, es necesario tomar decisiones estratégicas en toda la empresa”. A finales del año pasado, la empresa contaba con unos 16.000 empleados, de los cuales más de la mitad trabajaban en Estados Unidos. Lea más en Bloomberg.com
